# plugreports — full drug records
> 463 harm-reduction profiles, compiled from NIDA, DEA, EMCDDA, WHO and peer-reviewed literature. Street prices are regional estimates that change quickly. Educational information only — not medical advice. Canonical pages: https://plugreports.com/drugs/<slug>/

## Heroin
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/heroin/
- aliases: Dope, H, Smack, Sugar brown, Brown, Junk
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule I (US)
- appearance: White/off-white powder (US) or brown base powder ('sugar brown'); black tar (Mexico)
- effects: Rapid intense euphoria ('rush'); Warmth, heavy limbs; Pain relief, drowsiness ('nodding')
- risks: Extremely addictive — physical dependence in weeks; Overdose: breathing slows or stops; Unknown strength + fentanyl contamination
- overdoseSigns: Unresponsive, pinpoint pupils; Breathing <8/min or gurgling; Blue/gray lips and fingernails
- streetPrice: ~$10–$40 per bag; prices vary by region
- legalStatus: Illegal — Schedule I in the US; Class A (UK); controlled everywhere listed
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA, EMCDDA

## Fentanyl
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/fentanyl/
- aliases: Apache, China Girl, Dance Fever, Tango & Cash
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US, pharmaceutical)
- appearance: White powder, pressed pills, counterfeit oxycodone — often invisible when mixed into other drugs
- effects: Extreme euphoria; Drowsiness; Pain relief
- risks: Respiratory depression; Addiction in days; 2 mg (~a few grains) can be fatal
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Slow or stopped breathing; Blue lips, limp body
- streetPrice: ~$20–$40 per counterfeit pill
- legalStatus: Felony possession in all US states; analogues prosecuted under the Federal Analogue Act
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA, CDC

## Fentanyl HCl (powder)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/fentanyl-hcl/
- aliases: Fent HCl, China White (sold as)
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II / analogue prosecutions (US)
- appearance: Fine white crystalline powder, indistinguishable from other white powders
- effects: Same as fentanyl — opioid euphoria, sedation
- risks: Lab-purity powder is far stronger than street mixes; Weighing errors are fatal; Cross-contaminates everything it touches
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Respiratory arrest; Cyanosis (blue skin)
- streetPrice: ~$60–$120/gram wholesale equivalent; highly variable
- legalStatus: Illegal to possess without prescription; trafficking = federal felony
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: DEA, NIDA

## Acetylfentanyl
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/acetylfentanyl/
- aliases: ACE, Acetyl fent
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule I (US, 2015)
- appearance: White/tan powder, sometimes sold as 'synthetic heroin' or pressed into pills
- effects: Fentanyl-like opioid effects, shorter acting
- risks: ~5–15× weaker than fentanyl but still deadly at gram-level mistakes; Frequent cause of cluster overdoses
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Slow breathing; Loss of consciousness
- streetPrice: ~$25–$60/g where found
- legalStatus: Schedule I in the US; banned/controlled in EU, UK, Canada, Australia
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: DEA, EMCDDA, UNODC

## Furanylfentanyl (Fu-F)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/furanylfentanyl/
- aliases: Fu-F, FUF
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule I (US, 2018)
- appearance: White/yellowish powder or pressed tablets
- effects: Opioid euphoria and sedation, slower onset than fentanyl
- risks: Linked to hundreds of fatal overdoses 2016–2018; Potency similar to fentanyl
- overdoseSigns: Respiratory depression; Unconsciousness; Miosis (pinpoint pupils)
- streetPrice: ~$20–$50/g (residual availability)
- legalStatus: Schedule I (US); controlled in EU/UK/Canada/Australia
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: DEA, EMCDDA, NPS-AD

## Methoxyacetylfentanyl
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/methoxyacetylfentanyl/
- aliases: MAF
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule I (US, 2018)
- appearance: White/off-white powder
- effects: Powerful opioid sedation and euphoria
- risks: Potency comparable to or exceeding fentanyl; Tiny dosing errors fatal
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Slow/stopped breathing; Blue lips
- streetPrice: Rare; ~$30–$80/g where found
- legalStatus: Schedule I (US); controlled across EU, UK, Canada, Australia
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: DEA, EMCDDA

## Etonitazene
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/etonitazene/
- aliases: Etazene, EZ
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule I (US, 2023)
- appearance: White/yellow/off-white powder, pills, or e-liquid for vaping
- effects: Intense opioid euphoria at microgram doses
- risks: ~10–25× fentanyl potency; Active at sub-milligram doses — nearly impossible to dose safely
- overdoseSigns: Immediate respiratory depression; Unresponsiveness; Pinpoint pupils
- streetPrice: ~$40–$100/g (equivalent to millions of doses)
- legalStatus: Schedule I (US, 2023); controlled/prohibited in EU, UK, Canada, Australia
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: DEA, EMCDDA, WHO-UNODC

## Isotodesnitazene
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/isotodesnitazene/
- aliases: Iso, ISO
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Emerging — prosecuted as analogue (US); banned in several EU states
- appearance: White/yellow powder, often mixed into heroin or counterfeit pills
- effects: Euphoria, heavy sedation — nitazene-class opioid
- risks: Fentanyl-level or greater potency; Driving a new wave of overdose clusters since 2022
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Slow breathing; Blue lips
- streetPrice: ~$30–$70/g where found
- legalStatus: Analogue Act prosecutions (US); scheduled in DE/UK/others — check locally
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: EMCDDA, DEA, NPS-AD

## Oxymorphone (Opana 40 mg)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/oxymorphone/
- aliases: Opana, OM, Pink
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: Pink/octagonal ER tablets (Opana 40 mg); white IR tablets
- effects: Strong pain relief, euphoria, sedation
- risks: High addiction potential; Crushing ER tablets caused IV abuse epidemics and was withdrawn in US
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Respiratory depression; Loss of consciousness
- streetPrice: ~$30–$65 per 40 mg tablet (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule II; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: FDA, DEA, NIDA

## Morphine 60 mg
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/morphine-60mg/
- aliases: M60, MS Contin, Miss Emma
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: Round ER tablets imprinted 60 (purple/orange by brand); oral solution; injectable ampoules
- effects: Pain relief, calm, warmth; strong sedation at higher doses
- risks: Dependence within 2–3 weeks of daily use; ER tablets fatal if chewed/crushed
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Slow shallow breathing; Cold clammy skin
- streetPrice: ~$10–$30 per 60 mg tablet (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule II; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA

## Hydromorphone (Dilaudid 8 mg)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/hydromorphone/
- aliases: Dilaudid, D, Dillies, 8s
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: Small triangular white tablets ('8mg triangles'); clear injectable liquid
- effects: Rapid euphoria, warm sedation — 5× morphine potency
- risks: Fast IV addiction; Narrow safety margin; frequently implicated in overdose
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Respiratory depression; Unresponsiveness
- streetPrice: ~$20–$60 per 8 mg tablet (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule II; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA, CADTH

## Oxycodone (Roxicodone 30 mg)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/oxycodone/
- aliases: Roxy, 30s, Blues, Percs (with APAP), oxys, roxies
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: Blue 30 mg IR tablets; also white pills with various imprints
- effects: Euphoria, pain relief, energy then sedation
- risks: Highly addictive — a leading gateway to heroin/fentanyl transition; Counterfeit 'blues' are usually fentanyl
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Slow breathing; Blue lips
- streetPrice: ~$15–$40 per 30 mg tablet (diverted); $3–$15 for counterfeits
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule II; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA, CDC

## OxyContin
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/oxycontin/
- aliases: OC, Oxy, Hillbilly Heroin
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: Round ER tablets (OC imprint); reformulated 2010 to deter crushing
- effects: Long-duration pain relief and euphoria
- risks: Dependence; pre-2010 formulations still crushable on illicit market
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Respiratory depression; Sedation
- streetPrice: ~$20–$80 per 80 mg tablet (diverted; reformulated discounted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule II; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: FDA, NIDA

## Codeine 30/500 mg (co-codamol)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/codeine-30-500/
- aliases: T3s, Syrup, Lean (with promethazine)
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule V / Rx (US varies); OTC+pharmacy elsewhere
- appearance: White tablets (30 mg codeine / 500 mg paracetamol); purple/clear syrup
- effects: Mild euphoria, relaxation, cough suppression
- risks: Paracetamol component destroys the liver at high doses; Lean + alcohol risks fatal respiratory depression
- overdoseSigns: Extreme drowsiness; Slow breathing; Vomiting, confusion
- streetPrice: ~$2–$10 per tablet; $100+/pint syrup
- legalStatus: Rx-only in US (varies by state); pharmacy-controlled in EU; OTC-low-dose in some countries
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA

## Hydrocodone 10/500 mg
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/hydrocodone/
- aliases: Norco, Vicodin (with APAP), Watsons (Watson labs)
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US, since 2014)
- appearance: White/oblong tablets imprinted Watson 540-style; capsules historically
- effects: Pain relief, mild-moderate euphoria, sedation
- risks: Dependence; APAP liver toxicity when abused
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Slow breathing; Extreme drowsiness
- streetPrice: ~$5–$20 per 10 mg tablet (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule II; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: DEA, FDA

## Hydrocodone–Ibuprofen (Vicoprofen)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/vicoprofen/
- aliases: Vicoprofen, Ibu-hydro
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: White oblong tablets (7.5 mg hydro / 200 mg ibuprofen)
- effects: Pain relief, mild euphoria
- risks: Dependence; GI bleeding/renal harm at high ibuprofen doses
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Slow breathing; Confusion
- streetPrice: ~$5–$15 per tablet (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule II; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: FDA, DEA

## Meperidine (Demerol)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/meperidine/
- aliases: Demerol, Meperidine HCl caps, Pethidine
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: White capsules (50/100 mg); clear injectable solution
- effects: Short-acting euphoria and pain relief
- risks: Normeperidine metabolite causes seizures with repeated dosing; Outdated — largely replaced in medicine
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Respiratory depression; Tremor/seizures (toxic build-up)
- streetPrice: ~$5–$20 per 100 mg capsule (rare, diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule II; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: FDA, NIDA

## Methadone
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/methadone/
- aliases: Done, Dolly, Amidone, methalone
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: Orange/red diskettes (40 mg), liquid (cherry), tablets, injectable ampoules
- effects: Long-lasting (24–36 h) opioid stability, blocks withdrawal and cravings
- risks: Accumulates over days — overdose risk highest in first 2 weeks; Fatal mixing with benzos/alcohol
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Slow breathing; Extreme sedation
- streetPrice: ~$10–$40 per 40 mg diskette (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx via licensed opioid-treatment programs; diversion is a felony
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: SAMHSA, NIDA, DEA

## Suboxone (buprenorphine/naloxone)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/suboxone/
- aliases: Subs, Bupe, Strips, Oranges
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule III (US)
- appearance: Orange sublingual films (2/0.5 mg, 8/2 mg) or hexagonal tablets
- effects: Stops withdrawal and cravings; 'ceiling effect' limits respiratory depression
- risks: Dependence (milder than full opioids); Precipitates withdrawal if taken too soon after other opioids
- overdoseSigns: Rare alone; sedation + respiratory depression when mixed with benzos/alcohol
- streetPrice: ~$10–$25 per 8 mg film (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule III; felony without prescription (though widely used in treatment)
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: SAMHSA, FDA, NIDA

## Subutex (buprenorphine)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/subutex/
- aliases: Bupe, Subbies
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule III (US)
- appearance: White sublingual tablets (2 mg, 8 mg), hexagonal imprint
- effects: Long-acting opioid — treats withdrawal and pain
- risks: Diverted for IV use; Overdose when injected with depressants
- overdoseSigns: Sedation; Slow breathing (rare alone); Miosis
- streetPrice: ~$10–$30 per 8 mg tablet (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule III; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: SAMHSA, DEA

## Fentanyl patches (Duragesic 12.5 mcg/hr)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/duragesic/
- aliases: Duragesic, Patches, Gel patches
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: Tan rectangular transdermal patches (12.5–100 mcg/hr), gel or matrix type
- effects: 72-hour continuous pain relief; warmth amplifies absorption
- risks: Cut/heated patches dump lethal doses; A used patch still holds ~30–50% of its fentanyl
- overdoseSigns: Sedation; Slow breathing; Pinpoint pupils
- streetPrice: ~$20–$100 per patch (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule II; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: FDA, NIDA

## Diazepam
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/diazepam-drug/
- aliases: Valium, Bensedine, Apaurine (blue valium), V's
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule IV (US)
- appearance: 2–10 mg tablets (yellow/blue/white); Apaurine = blue 10 mg; clear injectable vials
- effects: Calm, muscle relaxation, anti-anxiety, sedation
- risks: Dependence in 2–4 weeks of daily use; Dangerous withdrawal (seizures) — never stop cold turkey; Mixing with opioids/alcohol can stop breathing
- overdoseSigns: Extreme drowsiness; Confusion; Slow breathing (especially with other depressants)
- streetPrice: ~$1–$10 per 10 mg tablet (diverted); counterfeits common
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule IV; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA, EMCDDA

## Alprazolam (Xanax 2 mg)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/alprazolam/
- aliases: Xanax, Bars, Pfizer LongBars, Zans, Footballs
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule IV (US)
- appearance: White 2 mg 'bars' (long, scored); blue/white/yellow football-shaped tablets by dose
- effects: Fast anti-anxiety relief; Calm sedation; Muscle relaxation
- risks: Dependence within weeks; brutal withdrawal (seizures risk); Counterfeit 'bars' increasingly contain fentanyl or bromazolam; Amnesia and risky behavior ('barred out')
- overdoseSigns: Extreme drowsiness; Slurred speech; Slow breathing — fatal with opioids/alcohol
- streetPrice: ~$2–$10 per 2 mg bar (diverted); $1–$5 counterfeits
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule IV; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA, EMCDDA

## Lorazepam (Ativan 2.5 mg)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/lorazepam/
- aliases: Ativan, Tranks, lorazap, lorazipam
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule IV (US)
- appearance: White tablets (0.5–2.5 mg) marked imprint; clear injectable vials (hospitals)
- effects: Calm, sedation, anti-anxiety, seizure control
- risks: Dependence and withdrawal seizures; Rebound anxiety between doses
- overdoseSigns: Extreme sedation; Confusion; Slow breathing with other depressants
- streetPrice: ~$1–$5 per 2.5 mg tablet (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule IV; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA

## Clonazepam (Rivotril/Klonopin 2 mg)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/clonazepam/
- aliases: Klonopin, Rivotril, K-pins, Super Valium (street)
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule IV (US)
- appearance: White/orange scored tablets (0.5–2 mg); Rivotril common in EU/LatAm
- effects: Long-acting calm, anti-anxiety, anti-seizure
- risks: Long half-life — dependence builds silently; Withdrawal can last months
- overdoseSigns: Extreme drowsiness; Slow breathing with mixes; Impaired coordination
- streetPrice: ~$1–$5 per 2 mg tablet (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule IV; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA

## Nitrazepam (Nipam 5 mg)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/nitrazepam/
- aliases: Nipam, Mogadon, Nitrazadon
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule IV (US) / Class C (UK)
- appearance: White 5 mg tablets (Nipam/Mogadon imprint)
- effects: Strong hypnotic — sleep induction, sedation
- risks: Morning 'hangover' impairment; Dependence and falls in older users
- overdoseSigns: Deep sedation; Slow breathing; Confusion
- streetPrice: ~$1–$4 per 5 mg tablet (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only; controlled in all target regions
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: EMCDDA, NHS

## Bromazepam (Lexotan 6 mg)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/bromazepam/
- aliases: Lexotan, Bromaz, Lexotanil
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule IV (US) / controlled EU
- appearance: Pink/red or white tablets (3/6 mg), 'Lexotanil 6' imprint
- effects: Anxiety relief, calm, moderate sedation
- risks: Dependence; withdrawal anxiety rebound
- overdoseSigns: Sedation; Slurred speech; Slow breathing in combination
- streetPrice: ~$1–$5 per 6 mg tablet (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only; controlled in US, EU, Canada, Australia
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: EMCDDA, DEA

## Etizolam
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/etizolam/
- aliases: Etiz, Etilaam, Etizest, Passionflower (branded)
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Not federally scheduled (US) — controlled in AL/AR/FL/OH/TX/VA etc.; banned UK 2017
- appearance: Pink/blue 1 mg tablets or pink round pellets ('pellets'); blotters
- effects: Fast anxiety relief and sedation, short-acting
- risks: Extremely popular RC benzo — dependence sneaks up fast; Fake 'Xanax' bars often contain etizolam or stronger analogues
- overdoseSigns: Sedation; Amnesia; Respiratory depression when mixed
- streetPrice: ~$0.50–$3 per 1 mg tablet/pellet
- legalStatus: Legal gray zone federally (US); illegal in UK, Germany, several US states; Rx in Italy/India/Japan
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: EMCDDA, TripSit, Erowid

## Clonazolam
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/clonazolam/
- aliases: C-lam, Clonitrazolam
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule I (US, 2023)
- appearance: White/pink powders, blotters, or pressed 'pellets' sold online
- effects: Very potent, long-lasting sedation and calm — active at ~0.5 mg
- risks: Potency ≈ 2–4× alprazolam; blackouts and delusions of sobriety; Withdrawal after short use due to potency
- overdoseSigns: Deep unconsciousness; Respiratory depression in mixes; Amnesia
- streetPrice: ~$1–$5 per 0.5 mg equivalent
- legalStatus: Schedule I (US, 2023); controlled/prohibited across EU, UK, Canada, Australia
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: DEA, EMCDDA, TripSit

## Diclazepam
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/diclazepam/
- aliases: Chlorodiazepam, 2'-chloro-diazepam
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Prosecutable under Analogue Act (US); banned UK 2017
- appearance: White powder or pellets; rarely seen as tablets
- effects: Long-acting (24–48 h) calm, muscle relaxation
- risks: Accumulation with repeated dosing; Protracted withdrawal
- overdoseSigns: Sedation; Impaired coordination; Slow breathing with mixes
- streetPrice: ~$1–$4 per pellet equivalent
- legalStatus: Analogue prosecutions (US); controlled in UK/EU; check locally
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: EMCDDA, TripSit

## Flubromazepam
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/flubromazepam/
- aliases: F-Pam, JYI 28
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Prosecutable as analogue (US); Class C (UK)
- appearance: White/off-white powder or 4–8 mg pellets/tablets
- effects: Very long-acting (up to 3 days) sedation and calm
- risks: Extreme duration — multi-day impairment and dangerous accumulation; Withdrawal can last weeks
- overdoseSigns: Prolonged sedation; Confusion; Slow breathing with other depressants
- streetPrice: ~$1–$5 per 4–8 mg equivalent
- legalStatus: Analogue Act (US); Class C UK; controlled in parts of EU
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: EMCDDA, TripSit, NPS-AD

## Flubromazolam
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/flubromazolam/
- aliases: F-Lam, JYI 73
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule I (US, 2023)
- appearance: White powder, blotters, pellets; active at ~0.25 mg
- effects: Ultra-potent, ultra-long sedative-hypnotic effects
- risks: Blackout doses are close to active doses; Detected in many fake-Xanax and fake-Valium supplies
- overdoseSigns: Unconsciousness; Respiratory depression; Days-long sedation
- streetPrice: ~$1–$4 per 0.25 mg equivalent
- legalStatus: Schedule I (US, 2023); controlled UK/EU/Canada
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: DEA, EMCDDA

## Flunitrazepam (Rohypnol)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/flunitrazepam/
- aliases: Rohypnol, Rophies, Roofies, Narcozep
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Not approved in US; Schedule IV-III equivalent elsewhere; 'date-rape drug' class
- appearance: White 1–2 mg tablets (old ones turned blue in drinks); clear odorless liquid
- effects: Heavy sedation, amnesia, muscle relaxation within 20–30 min
- risks: Anterograde amnesia — linked to drug-facilitated assault; 10× stronger hangover sedation than diazepam
- overdoseSigns: Total sedation; Confusion; Respiratory depression with alcohol — often fatal
- streetPrice: ~$2–$10 per 2 mg tablet where diverted
- legalStatus: Rx-only in ~60 countries; not manufactured for US; illegal without Rx everywhere on our list
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, UNODC

## Meclonazepam
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/meclonazepam/
- aliases: MBZ
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Analogue prosecutions (US); controlled several EU states
- appearance: White powder or pellets, 3–6 mg typical
- effects: Anxiolytic, muscle relaxant — clonazepam-like
- risks: Limited human data — unknown long-term harms; Dependence assumed class-typical
- overdoseSigns: Sedation; Motor impairment; Slow breathing with mixes
- streetPrice: ~$1–$4 per pellet equivalent
- legalStatus: Analogue Act (US); scheduled in parts of EU — check locally
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: TripSit, EMCDDA, NPS-AD

## Phenazepam
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/phenazepam/
- aliases: Phenaz, Bromdihydrochlorphenylbenzodiazepine
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Not scheduled federally (US) — state-level bans; Rx in Russia/CIS
- appearance: White 1–2.5 mg tablets (Russian pharma), or white powder
- effects: Long-acting strong anxiolytic/sedative; used for epilepsy in CIS
- risks: Linked to serious car crashes and deaths in CIS countries; Dose errors common with raw powder
- overdoseSigns: Deep sedation; Slow breathing; Amnesia
- streetPrice: ~$0.50–$3 per 1 mg tablet
- legalStatus: Rx in Russia/CIS; unscheduled federally in US (several state bans); controlled EU
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: EMCDDA, NPS-AD, TripSit

## Pyrazolam
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/pyrazolam/
- aliases: SH-I-04
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Analogue prosecutions (US); banned UK 2017
- appearance: White powder/pellets; active at 0.5–2 mg
- effects: Pure anti-anxiety with unusually little sedation (for a benzo)
- risks: Still dependence-forming; little euphoria drives redosing
- overdoseSigns: Sedation at high doses; Impairment; Slow breathing in mixes
- streetPrice: ~$1–$4 per mg-equivalent
- legalStatus: Analogue Act (US); Class C UK; check EU locally
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: TripSit, EMCDDA

## Zolpidem (Ambien/Stilnox)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/zolpidem/
- aliases: Ambien, Stilnox, Z-drugs, A-minus
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Schedule IV (US)
- appearance: White/pink oblong tablets (5–10 mg); 'Ambien' imprint
- effects: Sleep induction within 15 min; mild euphoria and amnesia at higher doses
- risks: Sleep-walking, sleep-driving, hallucinations; Dependence and rebound insomnia
- overdoseSigns: Extreme sedation; Confusion; Respiratory depression with other depressants
- streetPrice: ~$2–$10 per 10 mg tablet (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule IV; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: FDA, NIDA

## Secobarbital (Seconal)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/secobarbital/
- aliases: Seconal, Reds, Red devils, F-40s
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: Red-orange capsules (50–100 mg)
- effects: Rapid deep sedation, euphoria, disinhibition
- risks: Barbiturates: tiny margin between dose and death; Fatal in overdose, brutal withdrawal (seizures) — replaced by benzos in medicine
- overdoseSigns: Deep coma; Slow/absent breathing; Hypothermia, blisters
- streetPrice: ~$15–$40 per capsule where diverted (rare)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule II; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA

## Carisoprodol (Soma)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/soma/
- aliases: Soma, Carisoma, Vanadom
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Schedule IV (US, 2012)
- appearance: White 250/350 mg tablets; 'Soma' imprint
- effects: Muscle relaxation, sedation, mild euphoria (via meprobamate metabolite)
- risks: Converts to meprobamate (Miltown) — dependence; Popular 'Soma Coma' mix with opioids — deadly
- overdoseSigns: Extreme drowsiness; Low blood pressure; Slow breathing with opioids
- streetPrice: ~$1–$8 per 350 mg tablet (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule IV (US); OTC in some countries (Mexico)
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: DEA, FDA

## Cyclobenzaprine (Flexeril)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/cyclobenzaprine/
- aliases: Flexeril, Cyclobenz, Merck tabs
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Not scheduled (US)
- appearance: Yellow/orange 10 mg tablets (Merck); white 5 mg
- effects: Muscle relaxation, sedation; little euphoria
- risks: Overdose causes hallucinations, seizures, heart rhythm problems; Abuse usually in combination (potentiates opioids)
- overdoseSigns: Agitation then sedation; Fast/irregular heartbeat; Seizures, confusion
- streetPrice: ~$1–$5 per 10 mg tablet
- legalStatus: Rx-only (not federally controlled); prescription misuse is still illegal
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: FDA, NIH

## Pentobarbital (Nembutal)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/nembutal/
- aliases: Nembutal, Yellow jackets, Pentobarbs
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: Yellow capsules, pink injectable solution (veterinary), powder
- effects: Fast deep sedation → anesthesia
- risks: Veterinary euthanasia drug — overdose is usually fatal; Narrow safety margin (barbiturate)
- overdoseSigns: Coma; Absent breathing; Pupils dilated then fixed
- streetPrice: ~$30–$100+ per vial/capsule-equivalent (rare, diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule II; used in physician-assisted death in some jurisdictions under strict law
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: DEA, FDA

## GHB (gamma-hydroxybutyrate)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/ghb/
- aliases: G, Liquid ecstasy, Grievous Bodily Harm, Scoop
- category: GHB / GBL
- schedule: Schedule I/III (US — illicit GHB is I; approved drug Xyrem is III)
- appearance: Clear, salty/soapy-tasting liquid; white powder; clear capsules
- effects: Euphoria, disinhibition, increased sociability; sleep at higher doses
- risks: Dose curve is razor-thin — 1 mL too much = coma; Frequent dosing needed (90-min half-life) → dependence and brutal 24/7 withdrawal; Also linked to drug-facilitated assault
- overdoseSigns: Sudden deep sleep/unrousable; Vomiting while unconscious; Slow irregular breathing
- streetPrice: ~$5–$20 per dose (capful); ~$60–$150 per 100 mL where found
- legalStatus: Schedule I (illicit) US; Class B/C elsewhere — illegal without Rx everywhere listed
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, TripSit

## GHB Liquid
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/ghb-liquid/
- aliases: G liquid, Liquid G
- category: GHB / GBL
- schedule: Schedule I (US, illicit)
- appearance: Clear oily liquid in water bottles or vials; salty/soapy taste
- effects: Same as GHB — euphoria, disinhibition, sleep
- risks: Concentration unknown — strength varies bottle to bottle; Mixing with alcohol frequently fatal
- overdoseSigns: Unrousable sleep; Snoring/gurgling; Slow breathing
- streetPrice: ~$60–$150 per 100 mL (strength varies)
- legalStatus: Illegal without prescription (all target regions)
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA

## GHB Powder
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/ghb-powder/
- aliases: NaGHB, Sodium oxybate (pharma)
- category: GHB / GBL
- schedule: Schedule I (US, illicit); III for approved Xyrem
- appearance: White crystalline powder (hygroscopic)
- effects: Same as GHB liquid when dissolved
- risks: Dissolving errors → misdosing; Hygroscopic powder clumps — uneven concentration
- overdoseSigns: Coma-like sleep; Vomiting; Respiratory depression
- streetPrice: ~$40–$120 per 50 g where found
- legalStatus: Illegal without prescription (all target regions)
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA

## GBL (gamma-butyrolactone)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/gbl/
- aliases: GBL, Liquid gold, Blue nitro, Firestrip
- category: GHB / GBL
- schedule: Schedule I (US, 2000); controlled UK/EU/AU
- appearance: Clear liquid with chemical/cologne smell; industrial solvent
- effects: Converts to GHB in the body — euphoria, sedation
- risks: Stronger and faster than GHB; dosing even more unforgiving; Caustic — burns mouth/esophagus undiluted; Severe dependence with life-threatening withdrawal
- overdoseSigns: Deep unconsciousness; Slow breathing; Incontinence
- streetPrice: ~$50–$150 per liter (industrial-sourced)
- legalStatus: Schedule I (US); Class B UK; controlled EU/AU/CA — industrial chemical restrictions apply
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: EMCDDA, NIDA, Home Office

## Ketamine
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/ketamine/
- aliases: K, Special K, Kit Kat, Ketalar, ketmaine
- category: Dissociatives
- schedule: Schedule III (US)
- appearance: White crystalline powder; clear injectable liquid (Ketalar vials)
- effects: Dissociation (out-of-body), euphoria, pain relief; sedative at higher doses
- risks: Bladder damage (ketamine cystitis) with regular use; K-holes and accidents while impaired; Dependence with heavy use
- overdoseSigns: Unresponsive but eyes open; Slow breathing (rarely fatal alone); Vomiting while sedated
- streetPrice: ~$20–$60 per gram; vials $30–$100
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule III; illegal without prescription; Class B UK
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA

## Ketalar (ketamine injection)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/ketalar/
- aliases: Ketalar, Vials, K vials
- category: Dissociatives
- schedule: Schedule III (US)
- appearance: Clear liquid in 10/50 mg-per-mL vials, pharmaceutical packaging
- effects: Same as ketamine — dissociation, anesthesia
- risks: IV use raises infection and dependence risk; Bladder harm identical to powder use
- overdoseSigns: Deep sedation; Slow breathing with other depressants; Unresponsive
- streetPrice: ~$30–$100 per vial (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx/hospital-only, Schedule III; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: FDA, NIDA

## Cocaine
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/cocaine/
- aliases: Coke, Blow, Snow, Charlie, Yayo, Peruvian/Colombian
- category: Stimulants
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: White crystalline powder (HCl) or off-white 'base'/crack rocks; shiny 'fishscale' = high purity HCl
- effects: Euphoria, confidence, energy; Numbing (local anesthetic); Suppressed appetite and sleep
- risks: Heart attack/stroke even in young users; Severe addiction — craving cycle; Adulterants: levamisole (rotting flesh), fentanyl (overdose)
- overdoseSigns: Chest pain, racing irregular heartbeat; Seizures; Extreme agitation, overheating
- streetPrice: ~$60–$120 per gram (US); £40–£80 (UK); varies widely
- legalStatus: Schedule II (US); Class A (UK); illegal for non-medical use everywhere listed
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA, EMCDDA

## Speed (amphetamine paste)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/speed/
- aliases: Amphetamine, Base, Paste, Sulph, Whizz
- category: Stimulants
- schedule: Schedule II (US, as amphetamine)
- appearance: Damp white/yellowish paste or dry white powder; damp = high purity base
- effects: Energy, alertness, talkativeness; Appetite suppression; Euphoria at higher doses
- risks: Insomnia, anxiety, paranoia; Heart strain and overheating; Cut with caffeine, glucose, ephedrine, or worse
- overdoseSigns: Chest pain; Panic, hallucinations; Overheating, fast irregular pulse
- streetPrice: ~$10–$40 per gram (EU); £10–£30 (UK)
- legalStatus: Schedule II/controlled everywhere listed; Rx forms exist (Adderall, Dexedrine)
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, UNODC

## Methamphetamine
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/methamphetamine/
- aliases: Meth, Crystal, Ice, Glass, Tina, Crank
- category: Stimulants
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: Clear/white crystal shards ('ice'), powder, or pills
- effects: Intense euphoria, energy, focus lasting 6–12 h; Suppressed appetite/sleep; Confidence, hypersexuality
- risks: Addiction — among the most addictive drugs known; Meth mouth, skin sores, psychosis; Overdose: stroke, heart failure, overheating
- overdoseSigns: Chest pain, arrhythmia; Extreme agitation, paranoia; High fever, seizures
- streetPrice: ~$20–$100 per gram (US); varies by region
- legalStatus: Schedule II (US); Class A UK; illegal without Rx everywhere listed
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA, EMCDDA

## Ephedrine
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/ephedrine/
- aliases: Ephedra, Ma Huang, Mini-thins
- category: Stimulants
- schedule: Not scheduled (US) — regulated sale (combat-meth laws)
- appearance: White 25–30 mg tablets, powder, or dried herb
- effects: Stimulant, bronchodilator, appetite suppression
- risks: Heart palpitations, blood pressure spikes; Stroke at high doses; Pre-cursor to meth — heavily watched
- overdoseSigns: Racing heart; Tremor, anxiety; Severe hypertension
- streetPrice: ~$0.50–$3 per tablet (retail-regulated)
- legalStatus: OTC-regulated US (behind counter, ID + limits); Rx/controlled in many EU states
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: FDA, EMCDDA

## MDMA
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/mdma/
- aliases: Ecstasy (in pill form), Molly (powder), E, X, Adam
- category: Empathogens
- schedule: Schedule I (US)
- appearance: White/off-white crystals or powder ('Molly'); pressed pills with logos ('XTC')
- effects: Euphoria, empathy, emotional closeness; Energy, enhanced senses; Music/social enhancement
- risks: Overheating + dehydration (or fatal water intoxication); Serotonin depletion — multi-day comedown; Pills often contain PMA/PMMA (deadly) or cathinones
- overdoseSigns: Overheating, confusion; Racing heart, seizures; Jaw clenching, hallucinations
- streetPrice: ~$10–$40 per pill; ~$30–$80 per gram powder
- legalStatus: Schedule I (US); Class A UK; controlled everywhere listed
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA, EMCDDA

## Molly (MDMA powder)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/molly/
- aliases: Molly, Mandy (UK), Moon rocks
- category: Empathogens
- schedule: Schedule I (US)
- appearance: White/cream/purple-tinged crystalline powder or 'rocks'
- effects: Same as MDMA — euphoria, empathy, energy
- risks: 'Molly' is a marketing term, not a guarantee — half of seized 'Molly' contains other drugs; Overheating, serotonin syndrome with antidepressants
- overdoseSigns: Overheating; Confusion, seizures; Racing heart
- streetPrice: ~$30–$80 per gram
- legalStatus: Same as MDMA — Schedule I / Class A / controlled
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA

## XTC Pills (ecstasy tablets)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/xtc-pills/
- aliases: E pills, Beans, Rolls, Disco biscuits
- category: Empathogens
- schedule: Schedule I (US)
- appearance: Pressed tablets, every color/logo — Superman, Rolex, Tesla, skulls
- effects: 4–6 h euphoria, empathy, energy
- risks: High-dose pills (200–300+ mg) cause severe toxicity; PMA/PMMA masquerading as ecstasy has killed many users (slow onset → double-dosing)
- overdoseSigns: Body temperature >40°C / 104°F; Seizures, rigid muscles; Confusion, hallucinations
- streetPrice: ~$10–$40 per pill
- legalStatus: Schedule I (US); Class A UK; controlled everywhere listed
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, PillReports

## 5-APB
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/5-apb/
- aliases: Benzo Fury (with 6-APB blends)
- category: Empathogens
- schedule: Class B (UK); analogue prosecutions (US)
- appearance: White/brown powder or pellets
- effects: MDA-like empathy + stimulation, 6–10 h duration
- risks: Serotonin release + MAOI-like properties → serotonin syndrome risk; Long duration complicates dosing
- overdoseSigns: Overheating; Agitation, clonus; Racing heart
- streetPrice: ~$15–$40 per gram or ~$5–$15 per pellet
- legalStatus: Class B UK; Analogue Act US; controlled in parts of EU — check locally
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: EMCDDA, TripSit

## DMT (dimethyltryptamine)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/dmt/
- aliases: The Spirit Molecule, Deems, Dimitri, Businessman's trip
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Schedule I (US)
- appearance: White/yellow crystalline powder; also in ayahuasca plant brews
- effects: 5–20 min intense visual hallucinations, entity encounters; Altered sense of reality/time; Euphoria or terror
- risks: Psychological distress ('bad trips'); Dangerous behavior if unprepared; Raises heart rate/blood pressure
- overdoseSigns: No known lethal overdose in pure form — but terror/panic attacks are common; Fainting, vomiting
- streetPrice: ~$20–$60 per 50–100 mg dose
- legalStatus: Schedule I (US); Class A UK; controlled everywhere listed (plant/brew laws vary, e.g. religious exemptions in some countries)
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, DEA, MAPS

## Peyote (mescaline cactus)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/peyote/
- aliases: Lophophora williamsii, Buttons, Cactus
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Schedule I (US, except Native American Church ceremonial use)
- appearance: Small spineless grey-green cactus 'buttons'; dried slices
- effects: 8–12 h gentle visuals, introspection, euphoria; Nausea early on
- risks: Severe nausea/vomiting; Psychological distress; Slow-growing cactus — ecological harm from overharvesting
- overdoseSigns: No documented lethal overdose; Extreme nausea, disorientation
- streetPrice: ~$10–$30 per button where sold
- legalStatus: Schedule I (US) with NAC religious exemption; controlled in most target regions
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA

- overdoseSigns: No known lethal overdose; Vomiting, agitation

- overdoseSigns: Extreme agitation, hallucinations; Hypertension; Fever
- streetPrice: ~$10–$30 per pill or ~$50–$120 per gram
- legalStatus: Schedule I (US); controlled everywhere listed

## 4F-ADB
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/4f-adb/
- aliases: 4F-MDMB-BUTINACA
- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Schedule I (US, 2021)
- appearance: White/yellow powder sprayed onto plant material ('K2/Spice') or in vape carts
- effects: Cannabis-like high but far more intense — sedation, confusion, anxiety
- risks: Associated with 'Spice zombies' — catatonia, seizures; Unpredictable potency sprayed unevenly; Kidney damage, heart rhythm problems
- overdoseSigns: Severe agitation, psychosis; Seizures; Racing heart, vomiting

- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Schedule I (US)
- appearance: White powder sprayed on plant material or dissolved in e-liquid
- effects: Sedating, disorienting 'spice' high
- risks: Multiple deaths linked to 5F-ADB (the compound behind early 'zombie spice' outbreaks); Seizures, kidney injury
- overdoseSigns: Catatonic state; Seizures; Rapid heart rate
- streetPrice: ~$5–$20 per gram of blend

## AICAR (Acadesine)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/aicar/
- aliases: AICA ribonucleotide, GW501516's twin (grey market)
- category: Performance & Grey-Market Pharma
- schedule: Unscheduled (US/EU) — banned by WADA
- appearance: White powder, sold as 'exercise in a pill' grey-market research chemical
- effects: AMPK activator — increases endurance at cellular level (animal data only)
- risks: No human safety data — cancer-risk flags in cell studies; Sold as research chemical, zero quality control
- overdoseSigns: Unknown in humans; Potential hypoglycemia symptoms
- streetPrice: ~$50–$150 per gram (grey market)
- legalStatus: Unscheduled but not approved for human use; prohibited in sport (WADA)
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: WADA, PubMed

## Clenbuterol HCl
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/clenbuterol/
- aliases: Clen, Spiropent
- category: Performance & Grey-Market Pharma
- schedule: Not approved for human use (US); Rx elsewhere
- appearance: White 20–40 mcg tablets; veterinary liquid
- effects: Bronchodilator → fat loss, stimulant-like energy at higher doses
- risks: Racing heart, arrhythmia, tremors; Overdose: dangerous potassium shifts, cardiac events; Contaminated meat can cause positive tests
- overdoseSigns: Severe tremor; Racing irregular heart; Chest pain, dizziness
- streetPrice: ~$0.50–$2 per 40 mcg tablet (grey market)
- legalStatus: Not FDA-approved for humans (US); Rx veterinary/Rx human elsewhere; doping-banned
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: FDA, WADA

## Anastrozole (Arimidex)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/arimidex/
- aliases: Arimidex, Adex
- category: Performance & Grey-Market Pharma
- schedule: Rx-only (US/EU) — not a controlled drug
- appearance: White 1 mg tablets, 'Ari' imprints
- effects: Aromatase inhibitor — lowers estrogen (used in breast cancer; abused in steroid cycles)
- risks: Bone density loss, joint pain with long-term use; Crash estrogen too low → depression, libido loss
- overdoseSigns: Nausea, headache; Hot flashes
- streetPrice: ~$2–$8 per 1 mg tablet (grey market)
- legalStatus: Rx-only everywhere listed; not a controlled substance
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: FDA, EMA

## Tadalafil (Cialis)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/cialis/
- aliases: Cialis, Tadalis, Weekend pill
- category: Sexual Health & ED Meds
- schedule: Rx-only — not controlled
- appearance: Yellow almond-shaped 10/20 mg tablets; yellow film
- effects: 36-hour erectile enhancement
- risks: Counterfeit ED pills are a major fentanyl/adulterant channel in some regions; Dangerous blood pressure drop with nitrates
- overdoseSigns: Prolonged erection (>4 h — medical emergency); Chest pain, dizziness
- streetPrice: ~$2–$15 per tablet (counterfeit); Rx ~$10–$70
- legalStatus: Rx-only everywhere listed; large counterfeit trade
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12

## Potassium Cyanide (KCN)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/potassium-cyanide/
- aliases: KCN, Cyanide salts
- category: Hazardous Substances
- schedule: Not a drug — regulated toxic chemical (poisons laws)
- appearance: White crystalline salt, almond-like odor when damp
- effects: NONE — this is not a recreational drug. Blocks cellular oxygen use within minutes
- risks: Lethal dose ~200–300 mg — death within minutes to an hour; No antidote available outside hospital; hydrogen cyanide gas from acid contact
- overdoseSigns: All exposure is poisoning: gasping, seizures, collapse, cardiac arrest
- streetPrice: N/A — sometimes sold fraudulently as 'peaceful exit' scams
- legalStatus: Heavily regulated toxic chemical; possession without industrial license is a crime in all target regions
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: WHO, CDC, ATSDR

## Xylazine (Tranq)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/xylazine/
- aliases: Tranq, Tranq dope, Rompun (vet brand)
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Not a controlled drug — veterinary anesthetic, adulterant
- appearance: No street form of its own — found mixed into fentanyl/heroin (white/beige powder) or pills
- effects: Heavy sedation, slow breathing; Blackouts lasting hours; Severe skin wounds (eschar) at injection sites
- risks: Not an opioid — naloxone does NOT reverse it; it still kills breathing; Flesh-rotting wounds (tranq lesions) that lead to amputation; Withdrawal on top of opioid withdrawal, hard to treat
- overdoseSigns: Unresponsive with slow breathing; Blue-gray skin; Severe hypotension (very low blood pressure)
- streetPrice: Sold as part of fentanyl/heroin bags (~$10-$40) — no separate price
- legalStatus: Veterinary Rx-only; human use illegal; possession varies — often charged by drug weight when mixed
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-12
- sources: NIDA, CDC, DEA

## Cannabis (Weed)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/weed/
- aliases: Weed, Marijuana, Pot, Bud, Grass, Mary Jane, Ganja, Hash, THC
- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Schedule I (US federal) — legal or decriminalized in many states & countries
- appearance: Dried green/brown flower buds; hash/resin; oils & wax (concentrates); edibles; vape cartridges
- effects: Relaxation, euphoria ('high'); Altered senses, time perception; Increased appetite ('munchies')
- risks: Anxiety, panic attacks, paranoia — especially high-THC strains and concentrates; Impaired memory, coordination and driving ability for hours; Dependence with daily heavy use (~10–30% of users); withdrawal: irritability, insomnia; High-potency concentrates linked to psychosis episodes in vulnerable users; Illegal-market flower is sometimes contaminated with mold, pesticides, or sprayed synthetics ('spiked weed')
- overdoseSigns: No known fatal overdose — cannabis alone doesn't stop breathing; Severe panic attack, paranoia, racing heart; Cannabinoid hyperemesis: uncontrollable vomiting (relieved by hot showers); Fainting or extreme sedation when mixed with alcohol/other drugs
- streetPrice: ~$10–$20 per gram flower (US); far cheaper where legal; varies enormously
- legalStatus: Varies wildly: legal (Canada, Uruguay, many US states), decriminalized, or illegal — always check local law. Natural cannabis is NOT the same as synthetic cannabinoids ('Spice'), which are far more dangerous.
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-14
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, CDC

## Butorphanol (Stadol)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/butorphanol/
- aliases: Stadol, Torbugesic, Butomidor
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule IV (US)
- appearance: Clear nasal spray bottle or injectable vials (1–2 mg/mL); vet brands (Butomidor) common
- effects: Pain relief, mild euphoria; Sedation; Opioid-like relaxation
- risks: Dependence with regular use; Ceiling effect limits respiratory depression (safer than morphine family); Severe withdrawal if stopped abruptly after heavy use
- overdoseSigns: Sedation, confusion; Slow breathing (less pronounced than other opioids); Nausea, hallucinations at high doses
- streetPrice: ~$15–$40 per vial/nasal bottle (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule IV; veterinary diversion common
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-14
- sources: NIDA, FDA

## Butalbital (Fioricet/Fiorinal)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/butalbital/
- aliases: Fioricet, Fiorinal, Esgic
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Schedule III (US, combinations)
- appearance: White/blue tablets with caffeine + acetaminophen or aspirin (50/325/40 mg)
- effects: Sedation, relaxation; Tension-headache relief; Mild euphoria
- risks: Barbiturate dependence — tolerance builds in weeks; Rebound headaches drive overuse; Acetaminophen component destroys the liver at high doses
- overdoseSigns: Extreme drowsiness; Slow breathing; Confusion, slurred speech
- streetPrice: ~$2–$8 per tablet (diverted)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule III; online grey-market sales widespread
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-14
- sources: FDA, NIDA

## Flualprazolam
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/flualprazolam/
- aliases: Flualp
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule I (US, 2023); banned UK 2017
- appearance: White/off-white powder or pressed pellets; active at ~0.5 mg
- effects: Alprazolam-like calm and sedation, very potent; Long duration (8–12 h)
- risks: Detected in many fake 'Xanax' bars; Blackout window is wide — active and blackout doses are close; Withdrawal after short exposure due to potency
- overdoseSigns: Deep unconsciousness; Respiratory depression when mixed; Amnesia lasting hours
- streetPrice: ~$1–$4 per 0.5 mg-equivalent
- legalStatus: Schedule I (US, 2023); Class C UK; controlled across EU
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-14
- sources: DEA, EMCDDA

## Pregabalin (Lyrica)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/pregabalin/
- aliases: Lyrica, Nervigesic
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Schedule V (US); Class C (UK)
- appearance: White/orange/red-and-white capsules (75–300 mg)
- effects: Euphoria and calm at high doses; Nerve-pain relief; Reduced anxiety
- risks: Dependence and withdrawal (insomnia, anxiety, seizures); Mixing with opioids multiplies overdose risk; Popular in prisons; diverted heavily
- overdoseSigns: Extreme sedation; Slow breathing (especially with opioids); Blurred vision, confusion

## Zopiclone (Imovane)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/zopiclone/
- aliases: Imovane, Zimovane, Zop
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Rx-only; Class C (UK); unscheduled US (not FDA-approved)
- appearance: Blue film-coated tablets (3.75/7.5 mg); blisters branded 'ZOP'
- effects: Sleep within 30 min; Mild euphoria, amnesia at higher doses
- risks: Dependence and brutal rebound insomnia; Metallic taste, dry mouth; Sleep-walking and next-day impairment
- overdoseSigns: Deep sedation; Slow breathing with other depressants; Confusion, ataxia

## Opium
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/opium/
- aliases: Raw opium, Poppy latex, Afyon, Chandu
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US, tincture); opium itself Schedule I/II globally
- appearance: Dark brown/black sticky latex balls or bricks; tincture (laudanum) amber bottles
- effects: Morphine-like euphoria, warmth; Sedation, pain relief; Dreamy, nodding state

## Sufentanil

- category: Opioids

- appearance: Clear ampoules (5–50 mcg/mL), hospital-only packaging

- risks: 5–10× fentanyl potency — microgram dosing errors are fatal; Found in street fentanyl supplies; No field antidote beyond immediate naloxone + hospital care
- overdoseSigns: Instant respiratory arrest; Pinpoint pupils; Cyanosis

## Oxycodone–APAP (Percocet generic)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/oxycodone-apap/
- aliases: Percocet, Roxicet, Endocet, Camber oxy/APAP
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: White/yellow tablets (5/325, 10/325 mg) with various imprints; 'PERCOCET' brand bottle
- effects: Pain relief + euphoria like oxycodone alone; APAP adds no high — only liver risk
- risks: Acetaminophen liver failure when abused (max 4 g/day; abusers exceed quickly); Counterfeit 'Percocet' is a leading fentanyl pill; Dependence identical to oxycodone
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Slow breathing; Blue lips — treat as possible fentanyl overdose
- streetPrice: ~$5–$20 per 10/325 tablet (diverted); counterfeits $1–$5
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule II; felony without prescription
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-14
- sources: FDA, DEA

## Liraglutide (Saxenda)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/saxenda/
- aliases: Saxenda, Victoza, GLP-1 pen
- category: Performance & Grey-Market Pharma
- schedule: Rx-only — not a controlled drug
- appearance: Multi-dose injection pens (6 mg/mL), refrigerated
- effects: Appetite suppression, weight loss (GLP-1 agonist); No euphoria or recreational effect
- risks: Sold grey-market at huge markups with counterfeit/refilled pens; Nausea, pancreatitis risk; No high — scams sell water or insulin mislabeled as Saxenda/Ozempic
- overdoseSigns: Severe nausea/vomiting; Low blood sugar signs; Pancreatitis pain
- streetPrice: ~$200–$500 per pen grey-market (real Rx ~$1,300/mo US)
- legalStatus: Rx-only everywhere; massive counterfeit trade
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-14
- sources: FDA, EMA

## Naltrexone–Bupropion (Contrave)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/contrave/
- aliases: Contrave, Mysimba
- category: Performance & Grey-Market Pharma
- schedule: Rx-only — not controlled
- appearance: Blue tablets (8/90 mg), film-coated
- effects: Appetite suppression, mild stimulant effect (bupropion); Craving reduction (naltrexone)
- risks: Bupropion lowers seizure threshold; Misuse for stimulant-like effect is possible but weak; Grey-market 'weight loss' bundles pair it with thyroid hormone — dangerous
- overdoseSigns: Seizures; Racing heart, agitation; Severe nausea
- streetPrice: ~$1–$4 per tablet grey-market
- legalStatus: Rx-only; not a controlled substance
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-14
- sources: FDA, EMA

## Orforglipron (Foundayo)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/orforglipron/
- aliases: Foundayo, Oral GLP-1, Lilly GLP-1 pill
- category: Performance & Grey-Market Pharma
- schedule: Rx-only — not controlled; newly approved
- appearance: Small round tablets (0.25–12 mg), Lilly bottle
- effects: Once-daily oral GLP-1: appetite suppression, weight loss; No euphoria
- risks: Expect an immediate wave of counterfeit 'research' orforglipron — verify pharmacy accreditation; GI side effects, dehydration; Novel drug — long-term grey-market data nonexistent
- overdoseSigns: Severe vomiting/diarrhea; Dehydration, dizziness; Pancreatitis symptoms
- streetPrice: Pending launch; grey-market pre-orders already ~$100–$300/month
- legalStatus: Rx-only; newly approved — grey-market sales ahead of supply are almost certainly counterfeit
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-14
- sources: FDA, EMA

## Testosterone (injections & gels)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/testosterone/
- aliases: Test, Test C, Test E, Test P, Sustanon, Testogel, Cernos
- category: Steroids & Anabolics
- schedule: Schedule III (US, Rx); controlled in CA/UK/AU
- appearance: Vials of clear/yellow oil (cypionate, enanthate, propionate, Sustanon blends), transdermal gel sachets, undecanoate capsules
- effects: Muscle growth, strength, recovery; Libido and aggression changes; Elevated mood and energy at therapeutic doses
- risks: Shutdown of natural testosterone production (needs PCT); Cardiovascular strain, raised blood pressure, lipid damage; Gynecomastia (estrogen conversion), acne, hair loss; Grey-market vials routinely underdosed or mislabeled (independent lab tests)
- overdoseSigns: No acute 'overdose' — harm is cumulative; Severe hypertension, chest pain; Mood disturbance, aggression spikes
- streetPrice: ~$40–$80 per 10 mL vial grey-market; ~$10–$30 pharmacy-diverted
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule III (US); possession without Rx is a misdemeanor-to-felony depending on quantity/region
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: FDA, DEA, EMCDDA

## Trenbolone
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/trenbolone/
- aliases: Tren, Tri-Tren, Parabolan, Fina
- category: Steroids & Anabolics
- schedule: Not approved for humans anywhere (veterinary); controlled as anabolic in most regions
- appearance: Dark yellow vials (acetate/enanthate blends, 'Tri-Tren'); veterinary pellets historically refined
- effects: Extreme muscle growth and recomposition; Strength gains, hard 'dry' look; Insomnia, night sweats ('tren sweats'), vivid dreams
- risks: Harsh cardiovascular and lipid impact — among the most damaging AAS; 'Tren cough' — acute pulmonary reaction on injection; Aggression and mood disturbance ('tren rage' in some users); No legitimate human supply — all product is grey/black market
- overdoseSigns: No acute overdose; Severe hypertension, chest pain, arrhythmia; Acute breathing difficulty right after injection
- streetPrice: ~$50–$90 per 10 mL vial grey-market
- legalStatus: Illegal to possess for human use in US/UK/EU/AU; veterinary schedules apply
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: FDA, DEA

## Methandienone (Dianabol)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/dianabol/
- aliases: Dbol, Dianabol, Danabol, Anabol
- category: Steroids & Anabolics
- schedule: Schedule III (US); Class C (UK)
- appearance: Pink/blue 5–10 mg tablets (the classic 'Dbol' pinks), or 10–50 mg pills grey-market
- effects: Rapid mass and strength gains (water-retention heavy); Fullness and pump; Mood elevation, energy
- risks: Liver-toxic (17-alpha-alkylated) — hepatitis risk at high doses; Estrogen conversion: gynecomastia, bloating; Blood pressure and LDL damage; Counterfeit 'Dbol' frequently contains nothing or substitutes
- overdoseSigns: No acute overdose; Jaundice, dark urine (liver strain); Severe hypertension
- streetPrice: ~$30–$60 per 100 tablets grey-market
- legalStatus: Rx-only/controlled; the most-prescribed historic AAS, now mostly black/grey market
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: FDA, DEA

## Oxandrolone (Anavar)

- category: Steroids & Anabolics

- appearance: White 2.5–10 mg tablets, 'OXANDROLONE' imprints on pharma; capsules grey-market

- risks: Hepatotoxicity despite 'mild' reputation; HDL cholesterol crash; Expensive — the most-faked oral steroid; grey-market 'Var' is often Dianabol or Winstrol
- overdoseSigns: No acute overdose; Jaundice, fatigue (liver); Chest pain, hypertension

## Methyltrienolone (Oral Tren)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/oral-tren/
- aliases: Oral Tren, MTren
- category: Steroids & Anabolics
- schedule: Not approved for humans anywhere; controlled as anabolic
- appearance: 0.5–1 mg tablets or 1 mL vials — dosed in MICROGRAMS
- effects: Extreme potency per microgram — considered the strongest AAS; Rapid strength and recomposition
- risks: Catastrophically liver-toxic even at microgram doses; No human approval or dosing history — the risk ceiling is unknown; All supply is 'research chemical' grade with zero QC; Many users report immediate severe lethargy and liver values spiking
- overdoseSigns: No meaningful overdose margin exists; Jaundice, abdominal pain at almost any abuse dose; Hypertension
- streetPrice: ~$40–$80 per vial/bottle grey-market
- legalStatus: No legitimate human use; illegal grey-market research chemical
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: FDA, EMCDDA

## Sildenafil (Viagra)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/sildenafil/
- aliases: Viagra, Kamagra, Cenforce, Fildena, Vega
- category: Sexual Health & ED Meds
- schedule: Rx-only — not a controlled drug
- appearance: Blue diamond 25/50/100 mg tablets (Viagra); every color/shape from grey-market brands; oral jellies in sachets
- effects: Erection support on arousal (PDE5 inhibition, 30–60 min onset); Lasts ~4–5 hours; Also legitimately treats pulmonary hypertension (Revatio)
- risks: THE most counterfeited drug class in the world — fake sildenafil is a leading fentanyl-pill channel in some regions; Dangerous blood-pressure drop with nitrates (heart meds) — potentially fatal combo; Counterfeit pills: variable or zero active ingredient, contamination; Vision/color changes, priapism (4+ hr erection = medical emergency)
- overdoseSigns: Prolonged erection >4 hours — emergency; Severe dizziness, fainting (blood pressure drop); Vision or hearing loss — rare, urgent
- streetPrice: ~$1–$15 per tablet (grey-market generics vs pharmacy); counterfeits $0.50–$3
- legalStatus: Rx-only everywhere; massive counterfeit and grey-generic trade
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: FDA, EMA, Interpol

## Vardenafil (Levitra)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/vardenafil/
- aliases: Levitra, Staxyn, Vilitra, Valif
- category: Sexual Health & ED Meds
- schedule: Rx-only — not controlled
- appearance: Orange round 5/10/20 mg tablets (Levitra); grey-market brands in all colors; orodispersible forms
- effects: Erection support, 30–60 min onset; Slightly more potent per mg than sildenafil; Food affects it less than Viagra
- risks: Same nitrate danger as all PDE5 inhibitors (fatal BP drop); Counterfeit Levitra extremely common; QT-prolongation caution (heart rhythm) vs other PDE5s; Priapism, vision changes (same rare class effects)
- overdoseSigns: Prolonged erection >4 hours — emergency; Fainting, severe dizziness; Chest pain (never combine with nitrates)
- streetPrice: ~$1–$12 per tablet grey-market vs pharmacy
- legalStatus: Rx-only; heavily counterfeited
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: FDA, EMA

## BPC-157
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/bpc-157/
- aliases: Body Protection Compound, BPC
- category: Peptides & Research Chemicals
- schedule: Unscheduled — 'research chemical', not approved for human use anywhere
- appearance: White lyophilized powder in 2–10 mg vials, reconstituted with bacteriostatic water
- effects: Promoted for tendon/ligament healing and gut repair (animal data only); Anti-inflammatory reputation in biohacking communities
- risks: ZERO human clinical trials — all human use is anecdotal self-experimentation; Unregulated synthesis: purity, sterility, and actual content unverified; Unknown long-term effects including cancer-risk questions (growth-factor activity); Injecting 'research' vials carries infection and dosing-error risk
- overdoseSigns: Unknown in humans; Injection-site infection (redness, pus, fever); Allergic reaction

- legalStatus: 'Research use only' — selling for human consumption is illegal in US/EU; possession unscheduled
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16

## Somatropin (Human Growth Hormone)

- category: Hair Loss & Hormone Meds

## Finasteride (Propecia/Proscar)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/finasteride/
- aliases: Propecia, Proscar, Finax, Finpecia
- category: Hair Loss & Hormone Meds
- schedule: Rx-only — not controlled
- appearance: 1 mg (hair) and 5 mg (prostate) white tablets; film-coated brands
- effects: Stops and partially reverses male-pattern hair loss (DHT reduction ~65%); Shrinks enlarged prostate
- risks: Post-finasteride syndrome reports — persistent sexual dysfunction, depression, brain fog in a subset of users (debated but documented); Must be taken daily; gains reverse within a year of stopping; Depression warnings on labels in several countries; Women who are pregnant must not touch crushed tablets (birth defects)
- overdoseSigns: No acute overdose; Allergic reaction (rash, swelling)
- streetPrice: ~$0.30–$2 per tablet (generics cheap); grey-market 'research' versions unverified
- legalStatus: Rx-only; huge grey-generic market
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: FDA, EMA, NHS

## Tamoxifen (Nolvadex)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/tamoxifen/
- aliases: Nolvadex, Tamox, Nolva
- category: Hair Loss & Hormone Meds
- schedule: Rx-only — not controlled
- appearance: 10/20/40 mg white tablets, 'NOLVADEX' imprint
- effects: SERM — blocks estrogen at breast tissue (gyno protection); Standard PCT backbone for decades; Legitimate breast-cancer drug
- risks: Blood-clot risk (DVT/PE) — the serious one; Mood disturbance, hot flashes; Vision changes at high doses — retina concerns
- overdoseSigns: No acute overdose; Leg swelling/pain (clot) — emergency; Vision changes
- streetPrice: ~$0.50–$2 per 20 mg tablet grey-market
- legalStatus: Rx-only; universal PCT diversion
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: FDA, NHS

## Clomiphene (Clomid)

## hCG (Human Chorionic Gonadotropin)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/hcg/
- aliases: HCG, Pregnyl-style, HuCoG, Fertigyn
- category: Hair Loss & Hormone Meds
- schedule: Rx-only — not controlled (though listed in some sport bans)
- appearance: Lyophilized vials reconstituted for injection; '5000 IU' ampoules
- effects: Mimics LH — keeps testicles working during/after steroid cycles; Fertility preservation on cycle; Pregnancy hormone (the drug behind pregnancy tests)
- risks: Fake hCG is epidemic — most grey-market vials are underdosed or inert (and ironically the most-faked 'HGH' is often actually hCG); Gynecomastia if estrogen conversion spikes; Injection hygiene with multi-dose vials
- overdoseSigns: No acute overdose; Injection-site infection; Gyno onset
- streetPrice: ~$15–$40 per 5000 IU vial grey-market
- legalStatus: Rx-only; massive PCT diversion
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: FDA, WADA

## Minoxidil (Rogaine)

- appearance: 5% foam/solution bottles; oral 2.5–10 mg tablets (Rx legacy)

## IGF-1 & MGF analogues
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/igf-1/
- aliases: IGF-1 LR3, Somedin, PEG MGF, DES IGF
- category: Peptides & Research Chemicals
- schedule: Unscheduled — 'research chemicals'; IGF-1 is Rx (Increlex) in rare cases
- appearance: Lyophilized vials, 0.1–1 mg (microgram-dosed peptides)
- effects: Potent muscle-growth signaling (LR3 lasts ~20–30 h in the body); MGF variants marketed for repair

- overdoseSigns: Low blood sugar: shaking, sweating, confusion — eat sugar, seek help; Injection-site infection
- streetPrice: ~$30–$80 per vial grey-market
- legalStatus: 'Research use only'; not approved for performance use anywhere
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16

## Liothyronine (T3)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/t3-liothyronine/
- aliases: T3, Cytomel, Thyroxyl
- category: Weight Loss & Metabolic Meds
- schedule: Rx-only — not controlled
- appearance: 5/25/50 mcg tablets; grey-market 'research' versions

## Levothyroxine (T4)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/t4-levothyroxine/
- aliases: T4, Synthroid, Eltroxin, Levoxyl
- category: Weight Loss & Metabolic Meds
- schedule: Rx-only — not controlled
- appearance: 25–300 mcg tablets by many manufacturers
- effects: Standard hypothyroidism replacement — normalizes metabolism; Abuse: mild metabolic boost (must convert to T3 in the body, so weaker than T3 direct)
- risks: Overtreatment = hyperthyroid state: palpitations, anxiety, bone loss; Taking it without hypothyroidism provides little benefit at real risk; Interaction city — absorbs wrong with coffee, calcium, iron
- overdoseSigns: Racing heart, tremor, heat intolerance; Chest pain — emergency
- streetPrice: ~$0.10–$0.50 per tablet (cheap generic)
- legalStatus: Rx-only; the world's most-prescribed hormone
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: FDA, EMA

## Orlistat (Xenical/Alli)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/orlistat/
- aliases: Xenical, Alli, Orligal
- category: Weight Loss & Metabolic Meds
- schedule: OTC (60 mg, Alli) / Rx (120 mg) — not controlled
- appearance: Blue/white 60/120 mg capsules

- effects: Experimental 'fat-targeting' peptide — destroys blood supply to fat cells in animal studies; Dramatic primate weight loss (2011 study)
- risks: Never human-approved — kidney toxicity signals in early data; No dosing science for humans at all; The extreme-risk profile of an abandoned drug candidate
- overdoseSigns: Unknown — kidney stress would show as fatigue, swelling; Injection-site infection
- streetPrice: ~$50–$120 per vial grey-market
- legalStatus: 'Research use only' — abandoned candidate, not a supplement
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: PubMed

## Isotretinoin (Accutane)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/isotretinoin/
- aliases: Accutane, Roaccutane, Isotroin
- category: Performance & Grey-Market Pharma
- schedule: Rx-only with strict pregnancy-prevention programs (iPLEDGE US)
- appearance: 10/20/40 mg soft capsules; many generic brands
- effects: The definitive cystic-acne cure — shrinks sebaceous glands permanently; Often lifelong clearance after one course
- risks: TERATOGENIC — severe birth defects; pregnancy tests + two contraception forms required; Dry skin/lips/eyes (universal); Depression/suicidality association — debated but monitored; Grey-market acne 'brands' skip the monitoring that makes it safe
- overdoseSigns: No acute overdose; Severe headache, vision changes (pseudotumor cerebri — emergency); Mood crisis
- streetPrice: ~$0.50–$2 per capsule grey-market (pharmacy $100s/course)
- legalStatus: Rx-only, pregnancy-category-X protocols; grey market skips safeguards
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: FDA, EMA

## Modafinil (Provigil)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/modafinil/
- aliases: Provigil, Modalert, Modvigil, Modasmart
- category: Performance & Grey-Market Pharma
- schedule: Schedule IV (US)
- appearance: 100/200 mg white tablets; grey 'smart drug' versions ubiquitous
- effects: Wakefulness — promotes alertness without classic stimulant jitter; Shift-work/narcolepsy indication; off-label focus use
- risks: Headache (most common); Serious rash — Stevens-Johnson syndrome (rare, dangerous); Anxiety, insomnia; BP elevation; Grey 'Modasmart' etc. — content variance unknown
- overdoseSigns: Agitation, insomnia, racing heart; Severe rash — emergency (SJS)
- streetPrice: ~$1–$3 per 200 mg grey-market
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule IV (US); prescription-only EU/UK/AU
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: FDA, EMA

## Salbutamol (Albuterol/Ventolin)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/salbutamol/
- aliases: Albuterol, Ventolin, Asthalin, ProAir
- category: Performance & Grey-Market Pharma
- schedule: Rx-only (US) / OTC+pharmacy elsewhere (UK pharmacy, AU OTC)
- appearance: Blue MDI inhalers (100 mcg/puff), respules for nebulizers
- effects: Instant bronchodilation — relieves asthma attacks in minutes; Grey-market use: stimulant-adjacent 'cutting' aid and clenbuterol alternative
- risks: Tremor, racing heart at high doses; Potassium drop (hypokalemia) — dangerous with cardiac conditions; Counterfeit inhalers deliver wrong doses — genuinely dangerous for asthmatics; Used by bodybuilders as a 'safer clen' — the margin isn't as wide as assumed
- overdoseSigns: Racing irregular heart, tremor; Chest pain — emergency; Severe headache (BP)
- streetPrice: ~$5–$20 per inhaler grey-market; respules ~$1–3
- legalStatus: Rx/OTC varies; widely diverted
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: FDA, NHS

- streetPrice: ~$0.10–$0.50 per tablet (cheap generic)

- appearance: 10–80 mg tablets; white ovals

## Dapoxetine & combo pills
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/dapoxetine/
- aliases: Priligy, Super Kamagra, Extra Super P-Force, Tadapox
- category: Sexual Health & ED Meds
- schedule: Rx-only (approved in ~50 countries, not US FDA)
- appearance: 30/60 mg tablets; combo pills pair it with sildenafil/tadalafil/vardenafil
- effects: Short-acting SSRI — delays ejaculation (premature ejaculation treatment); Combos: erection aid + delay in one pill
- risks: Serotonin syndrome risk — especially with real antidepressants, MDMA, or other serotonergic drugs; Syncope (fainting) — the labeled warning; take with water, standing up slowly; Combos stack PDE5 + SSRI hypotension — dizziness is common; Counterfeit combos: unpredictable ratios
- overdoseSigns: Fainting, severe dizziness; Agitation, fever, sweating (serotonin syndrome) — emergency; Racing heart
- streetPrice: ~$1–$4 per combo tablet grey-market
- legalStatus: Rx-only in approved countries; grey market elsewhere
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16

## Steroid blend products
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/steroid-blends/
- aliases: Cut Stack, Tren/Test 350, Hexaplex, Ultraplex, Superbolan, KLOW
- category: Steroids & Anabolics
- schedule: Unapproved designer mixtures — controlled as anabolics
- appearance: Multi-compound vials (e.g., test + tren + masteron in one oil), labeled with total mg/mL
- effects: Convenience: several compounds in one injection; Marketing: 'custom blends' for cutting/bulking
- risks: You can't adjust individual compounds — dosing one means dosing all; Mislabeling is rampant: lab tests find wrong compound ratios or entirely different steroids; Allergic reactions to multi-ester brews; No pharmaceutical equivalent — every blend is grey-market
- overdoseSigns: No acute overdose; Injection-site infection, abscess; Severe post-injection pain ('test flu' amplified)
- streetPrice: ~$50–$90 per 10 mL vial grey-market
- legalStatus: Unapproved mixtures; illegal as anabolics; zero QC
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
