## Poppers (Alkyl Nitrites)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/poppers/
- aliases: Amyl nitrite, Amyl, Rush, Jungle Juice, Liquid Gold, Isobutyl nitrite
- category: GHB / GBL
- schedule: Legal to possess (UK, much of EU); Rx-only pharmaceutical amyl in US; regulated variously
- appearance: Small amber/blue bottles (10–30 mL) of volatile liquid; sold as 'room odorizer', 'leather cleaner', 'video head cleaner'
- effects: Instant head-rush warmth and euphoria (10–30 seconds); Muscle relaxation — especially smooth muscle; Enhanced skin sensation; disinhibition; Briefly drops blood pressure, dilates blood vessels
- risks: Fatal blood-pressure crash when combined with Viagra/Cialis/Levitra (PDE5 inhibitors) — the classic killer combo; Methemoglobinemia at heavy/repeated use — blood stops carrying oxygen (blue lips, breathlessness); Skin burns around nose/mouth from contact; Vision damage ('poppers maculopathy') — documented, sometimes permanent; Headache, fainting, nausea common; rebound blood-pressure spikes
- overdoseSigns: Blue/gray lips and skin (methemoglobinemia); Fainting, extreme dizziness; Racing heart then collapse; Breathing difficulty
- streetPrice: ~$5–$20 per bottle; ~$10–$30 online
- legalStatus: Possession largely legal (UK, EU, AU); amyl nitrite Rx-only in US but butyl/isobutyl variants sold openly; sales for human consumption banned in some places — sold as 'cleaners'
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: EMCDDA, NHS, PubMed

## THC Vapes & Carts
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/thc-vapes/
- aliases: Weed vape, THC cart, Dab pen, Cannabis vape, 510 carts
- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Schedule I (US federal, where cannabis illegal); legal-market versions in legal states/countries
- appearance: 510-thread cartridges (clear oil, various colors), disposable pens, pod systems; black-market carts often darker/thicker
- effects: Fast onset (2–5 min) — cleaner high than smoking for many; Discreet, low odor; Precise dosing on legal devices
- risks: EVALI — the 2019 lung-injury outbreak: black-market carts cut with vitamin E acetate destroyed lungs; thousands hospitalized, dozens died; Counterfeit packaging ('Dank Vapes', fake California labels) is near-total in illegal markets; High-THC concentrates (80–95%) — dependence and psychosis risk higher than flower; Heavy-metal leaching from cheap cartridges into the oil; No regulation in illegal markets: pesticides, solvents, synthetics
- overdoseSigns: No fatal overdose from THC alone; Severe anxiety, panic, paranoia; Fainting, vomiting (especially with alcohol); Psychotic episode in predisposed users
- streetPrice: ~$20–$60 per cart illegal market; legal-market $30–$80; disposables $25–$60
- legalStatus: Varies with cannabis law — illegal carts sold everywhere regardless; EVALI risk applies to all unregulated carts
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: CDC, FDA, NIDA

## Cannabis Edibles (THC/CBD)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/thc-edibles/
- aliases: Edibles, Gummies, THC chocolate, Cannabis-infused food, CBD edibles
- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Follows local cannabis law; unregulated market where illegal
- appearance: Gummies, chocolates, baked goods, drinks; legal-market labeled dosing (5–10 mg), black-market often unlabeled or 50–100 mg+
- effects: Slow onset (30 min–2 h), long duration (4–8 h); Body-heavy high, stronger than smoking at equivalent dose; CBD versions: relaxation without the high (at real doses)
- risks: THE classic overdose: people eat more when it 'isn't working yet' — 2–3 hour delay means stacking doses; Overconsumption: severe panic, paranoia, vomiting — miserable but not life-threatening; Children/pets eating gummies — poison-center calls spike wherever edibles are legal; Black-market edibles: unlabeled or wildly mislabeled THC content; Food-safety issues in unregulated kitchens
- overdoseSigns: No fatal overdose alone; Extreme anxiety, paranoia, hallucinations; Vomiting, inability to stand; Racing heart — usually panic, not cardiac emergency
- streetPrice: Legal market: $2–$5 per 10 mg dose; black-market gummies $5–$20; homemade variable
- legalStatus: Legal in cannabis-legal jurisdictions with labeling rules; illegal elsewhere — but universally available
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: CDC, NIDA, Poison Control

## Psilocybin Mushrooms (Shrooms)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/psilocybin-mushrooms/
- aliases: Magic mushrooms, Shrooms, Psilocybe, Gold caps, Liberty Caps
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Schedule I (US); Class A (UK); decriminalized in some US cities/states, legal in Jamaica/Brazil/parts of NA
- appearance: Dried whole mushrooms (golden-brown caps, blue-stem bruising), or ground into chocolate/tea; 'magic truffles' (sclerotia) in NL
- effects: 4–6 hour psychedelic trip: visual patterns, altered thinking, euphoria or introspection; Enhanced senses, time distortion; 'Mystical' experiences at sufficient doses
- risks: The bad trip: intense panic, paranoia, terror — psychological harm without physical toxicity; Dangerous behavior when impaired (traffic, heights, water); Triggering psychosis in predisposed individuals; Lookalike poisoning — wild mushrooms misidentified (the real physical danger); Disorientation leading to accidents, hypothermia, self-harm in rare cases
- overdoseSigns: No known lethal dose of pure psilocybin (LD50 extremely high); Extreme panic/agitation ('freaking out'); Confusion, inability to recognize surroundings; Vomiting, diarrhea (especially lookalike poisoning — emergency)
- streetPrice: ~$8–$15 per gram dried (typical dose 1–3.5 g); truffles ~€10–€20 per dose
- legalStatus: Schedule I US, Class A UK, illegal most regions; decriminalized (not legal) in some US jurisdictions; legal/gray in Jamaica, Brazil, Netherlands (truffles), parts of North America
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-16
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, MAPS

## Nitrous Oxide (Whippets / Galaxy Gas)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/nitrous-oxide/
- aliases: Whippets, Whip-its, Laughing gas, NOS, Galaxy Gas, Balloons, Hippy crack
- category: GHB / GBL
- schedule: Legal to possess (UK); food-grade legal, psychoactive sales banned (UK Psychoactive Substances Act)
- appearance: Small silver 8g chargers, large 500–640g 'Galaxy Gas' canisters (flavored), balloons filled with gas
- effects: 30–60 second euphoria, giggling, floating; Dissociation, sound distortion; Brief numbness and warmth
- risks: VITAMIN B12 DESTRUCTION — the signature harm: inactivates B12, causing progressive numbness, tingling, weakness, and in heavy users PERMANENT nerve damage ('drop foot', inability to walk); Oxygen deprivation — 100% nitrous displaces oxygen; unconsciousness and death; Frostbite on lips/lungs from direct gas contact; B12-deficiency anemia; Psychological dependence — daily users report craving the brief escape
- overdoseSigns: Blue lips/face (oxygen deprivation); Unconsciousness, unrousable; Seizures; Chest pain, irregular heartbeat
- streetPrice: ~$1–$3 per 8g charger; Galaxy Gas canisters $25–$60; festival balloons $5–$10
- legalStatus: Possession legal most places; UK banned psychoactive nitrous sales (2023); driving under influence illegal; sale to minors restricted
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, CPSC

## Whippets (Whipped Cream Chargers)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/whippets/
- aliases: Whip-its, Chargers, Nangs, Nos
- category: GHB / GBL
- schedule: Food-grade product — no regulation as drug until abused
- appearance: Small silver metal cartridges (the 'cracker' or charger), sold for whipped cream dispensers
- effects: Identical to nitrous oxide — brief 30–60s euphoria; Lightheadedness, giggling
- risks: Same as nitrous: B12 destruction and nerve damage with regular use; Extremely accessible — sold openly to minors; Cold gas burns to throat/lungs; Repeated use in one session = oxygen deprivation risk; Often the FIRST drug middle-schoolers try
- overdoseSigns: Unconsciousness; Blue lips; Seizures; Irregular heartbeat
- streetPrice: ~$1–$3 per charger; boxes of 24 for $20–$40
- legalStatus: Legal product (whipped cream propellant); abuse not specifically criminalized most places; sale restrictions to minors in some jurisdictions
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: NIDA, CPSC, drugfree.org

## Air Duster (Computer Duster / Canned Air)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/air-duster/
- aliases: Dusting, Duster, Canned air, Keyboard cleaner, Dust-Off
- category: Hazardous Substances
- schedule: Household product — not a drug; no age restriction on purchase
- appearance: Aerosol cans of difluoroethane/tetrafluoroethane sold as electronics/computer cleaner
- effects: Brief 10–30 second euphoria, disorientation; Feeling of floating, slurred speech
- risks: SUDDEN SNIFFING DEATH — the most deadly inhalant: difluoroethane sensitizes the heart to adrenaline; a sudden fright, chase, or exertion triggers fatal cardiac arrest. First-time users die; Frostbite to lungs and airway from direct spray; Brain damage from oxygen deprivation; Loss of consciousness with bag over head = suffocation; Completely legal, cheap, and in every home/school
- overdoseSigns: Sudden collapse, cardiac arrest; Seizures; Irregular heartbeat then death; Choking/vomiting while unconscious
- streetPrice: $3–$8 per can at any electronics/office store
- legalStatus: Household product; inhalant abuse laws vary; no purchase restriction — the 'perfect storm' accessible killer
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: CPSC, NIDA, drugfree.org

## Gasoline / Petrol Huffing
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/gasoline-huffing/
- aliases: Huffing gas, Petrol sniffing, Chrome
- category: Hazardous Substances
- schedule: Not a drug — fuel product
- appearance: Liquid gasoline/petrol, inhaled from cans, rags, or bags
- effects: Brief euphoria, disorientation, dizziness; Loss of coordination, slurred speech
- risks: Extremely toxic hydrocarbons (benzene, toluene, xylene); Sudden sniffing death — cardiac arrest; PERMANENT brain damage — toluene destroys myelin; chronic users develop dementia-like syndrome; Kidney/liver damage; Lead poisoning from leaded fuel (still used some regions)
- overdoseSigns: Sudden collapse; Seizures; Irregular heartbeat; Chemical burns around mouth
- streetPrice: Effectively free — siphoned fuel
- legalStatus: Not a drug; inhalant abuse criminalized in some places
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA

## Glue / Solvent Sniffing
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/glue-sniffing/
- aliases: Huffing glue, Solvents, Toluene sniffing, Chroming
- category: Hazardous Substances
- schedule: Not drugs — adhesives and solvents
- appearance: Household glue (model glue, rubber cement), paint thinner, correction fluid, felt-tip markers
- effects: 10–15 min euphoria, disinhibition, hallucinations; Dizziness, slurred speech, loss of coordination
- risks: The CLASSIC youth inhalant — peak use age 14–15; Sudden sniffing death from cardiac arrest; Permanent brain damage (cerebellar atrophy — users lose ability to walk/talk); Liver, kidney, heart damage; Suffocation from bag over head; 'Huffer's rash' around the mouth — telltale sign
- overdoseSigns: Sudden collapse, cardiac arrest; Seizures; Unconsciousness; Irregular heartbeat
- streetPrice: $1–$5 per tube/can — pocket money prices
- legalStatus: Legal products; abuse is the danger
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17

- appearance: Compressed refrigerant gas from air conditioners, freezers, coolant cans

## Tianeptine (Gas Station Heroin)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/tianeptine/
- aliases: ZaZa, Tiana, Neptune's Fix, Pegasus, TD Red
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Not federally scheduled (US) — FDA warnings; banned in some states (2023-2024)
- appearance: Capsules, tablets, or liquid shots sold at gas stations, vape shops, online as 'dietary supplement'
- effects: Opioid-like euphoria, warmth, relaxation at high doses; At prescribed doses (Europe): antidepressant effect

- overdoseSigns: Respiratory depression (slow/stopped breathing); Coma; Seizures; Pinpoint pupils, blue lips
- streetPrice: ~$15–$40 per bottle (30–90 capsules); shots $10–$20

## Kratom (Mitragyna speciosa)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/kratom/
- aliases: Ketum, Thang, Kakuam, Biak
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Not federally scheduled (US) — FDA warnings; illegal in 6+ states; banned Thailand (re-legalized 2021), some EU
- appearance: Green powder, capsules, extracts, liquid shots sold at smoke shops/gas stations
- effects: Low dose: stimulant energy, focus; High dose: opioid-like sedation, pain relief; Mitragynine acts on opioid receptors
- risks: Opioid-like dependence and withdrawal (insomnia, muscle aches, irritability, diarrhea); FDA links to seizures, liver damage, hallucinations; Salmonella contamination — 2018 outbreak, 35+ deaths linked to tainted kratom; Unregulated products — unknown alkaloid content, contamination; Naloxone DOES reverse kratom overdose (opioid receptor activity); Gateway to opioid use for some
- overdoseSigns: Seizures; Respiratory depression (high doses); Liver injury signs (jaundice, dark urine); Hallucinations, confusion
- streetPrice: ~$10–$30 per ounce powder; extracts $20–$50; shots $8–$15
- legalStatus: Not federally scheduled; illegal in Alabama, Arkansas, Indiana, Rhode Island, Vermont, Wisconsin; FDA warns against all use
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: FDA, Mayo Clinic, NIDA

## Phenibut
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/phenibut/

- category: GHB / GBL
- schedule: Not scheduled US (sold as supplement — illegally); Rx in Russia/Latvia
- appearance: White powder, capsules, or 'smart drug' blends sold online/gas stations
- effects: Anxiety reduction, sociability, mild euphoria; At high doses: sedation, disinhibition
- risks: RAPID TOLERANCE — daily use creates dependence in 2–3 weeks; Withdrawal is BRUTAL and dangerous: severe anxiety, insomnia, hallucinations, psychosis, seizures — worse than benzodiazepine withdrawal for some; Overdose: severe sedation, respiratory depression (especially with alcohol/opioids); Not reversed by naloxone; Sold as 'nootropic supplement' — no regulation, no quality control

## Delta-8 THC
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/delta-8-thc/
- aliases: D8, Delta-8, Diet weed, Hemp THC
- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Federally unscheduled (2018 Farm Act loophole); banned in 20+ states
- appearance: Gummies, vapes, tinctures, flower sprayed with D8 distillate — sold at gas stations, smoke shops
- effects: Milder high than Delta-9 THC: relaxation, euphoria; Edibles can be surprisingly potent
- risks: UNREGULATED — 2021-2023 testing found residual solvents, heavy metals, and unknown byproducts in many D8 products; Conversion process (CBD→D8) uses harsh acids/solvents; Psychoactive — impaired driving, anxiety, psychosis at high doses; Pediatric poisonings from gummies; Many states banned it — legality is a patchwork
- overdoseSigns: Extreme anxiety, paranoia; Vomiting; Fainting; Hallucinations (high doses)
- streetPrice: ~$10–$40 gummies; vapes $20–$50; flower $15–$30/8th
- legalStatus: Federally unscheduled (hemp loophole); banned in 20+ states including NY, CO, WA, CA (ironically stricter than D9 states)
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: FDA, CDC, NIDA

## HHC (Hexahydrocannabinol)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/hhc/
- aliases: HHC, Hexahydrocannabinol, Hydroxyhexahydrocannabinol
- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Federally unscheduled; state bans spreading
- appearance: Vapes, gummies, distillate — semi-synthetic cannabinoid from hemp CBD
- effects: THC-like high: euphoria, relaxation; Often described as between D8 and D9 in strength
- risks: Semi-synthetic — hydrogenation process uses metal catalysts (palladium, platinum) with contamination risk; ZERO human safety research; Unregulated products — unknown purity; Impaired driving, anxiety, dependence; Drug tests: may or may not trigger (metabolites uncertain)
- overdoseSigns: Anxiety, paranoia; Vomiting; Fainting; Racing heart
- streetPrice: ~$20–$50 vapes; gummies $15–$40
- legalStatus: Federally unscheduled (hemp-derived); banned in some states; 'legal high' grey market
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: FDA, EMCDDA

## THC-O Acetate
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/thc-o-acetate/
- aliases: THC-O, THC-O-A, Psychedelic THC
- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Federally unscheduled; DEA considers it illegal (2023); banned multiple states
- appearance: Vapes, gummies, tinctures — synthetic 'super THC'
- effects: 3× stronger than Delta-9 THC; Psychedelic-like effects at high doses: visual distortions, spiritual experiences
- risks: EXTREMELY potent — overdose risk far higher than regular THC; Acetylation process uses acetic anhydride — industrial chemical contamination; DEA ruled THC-O is a Schedule I controlled substance (2023) — despite being sold openly; Severe anxiety, psychosis, hospitalizations reported; Unregulated production
- overdoseSigns: Severe anxiety, panic, paranoia; Hallucinations; Vomiting, inability to stand; Psychotic episodes
- streetPrice: ~$25–$60 vapes; gummies $20–$50
- legalStatus: DEA: Schedule I (2023) — illegal federally despite hemp origin; many states banned independently

## Salvia Divinorum
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/salvia-divinorum/
- aliases: Salvia, Diviner's sage, Sally D, Magic mint
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Legal federally (US); illegal in ~20 states; Class A UK (2021)
- appearance: Dried leaf, extracts (5×–60×), liquid tinctures; smoked or chewed
- effects: 5–15 min INTENSE dissociation: out-of-body, entity contact, time distortion; Loss of physical coordination, uncontrollable laughter or terror
- risks: EXTREMELY disorienting — users hurt themselves falling, walking into objects, or wandering into danger; Terrifying experiences ('bad trips') with lasting psychological impact; Loss of reality contact — accidents, self-harm during acute phase; No physical overdose, but behavioral danger is extreme; Not a party drug — Mazatec shamans used it with a sitter for a reason
- overdoseSigns: No lethal dose — but total loss of motor control; Screaming, panic, fleeing; Self-injury without awareness; Post-experience anxiety, derealization
- streetPrice: ~$10–$30 per gram leaf; extracts $20–$60
- legalStatus: Legal federally (US) but illegal in ~20 states; Class A drug UK (2021); regulated Australia, much of EU
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA

## DXM (Dextromethorphan / Robotripping)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/dxm/
- aliases: Robo, Triple C, Skittles, Dex, Poor man's PCP
- category: Dissociatives
- schedule: OTC (unscheduled) — no purchase age federal US (18 in some states/stores)
- appearance: Cough syrup, gel caps, tablets (Coricidin Cough & Cold, Robitussin, Delsym)
- effects: Dissociation: out-of-body, floating, robot-walk at high doses; Plateaus 1–4: euphoria → dissociation → complete detachment → ego death
- risks: Serotonin syndrome — DXM is serotonergic; DEADLY with SSRIs, MAOIs, MDMA; Liver damage — Coricidin contains chlorpheniramine (antihistamine) that's hepatotoxic at abuse doses; Dissociation injuries — users hurt themselves while out-of-body; Hot and dehydrated at high doses; OTC = easy teen access; 'robo-tripping' popular with 12–17 age group
- overdoseSigns: Severe dissociation, unresponsiveness; Racing heart, high blood pressure; Hyperthermia; Seizures (serotonin syndrome combo)
- streetPrice: ~$5–$12 per bottle (OTC); pure DXM powder $20–$40/g online
- legalStatus: OTC — no federal purchase age; 18+ in some states/stores; bulk pure DXM restricted
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: NIDA, Poison Control

## Benadryl (Diphenhydramine) Abuse
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/benadryl-abuse/
- aliases: Benny, Bennies, DPH, Sleep-away
- category: Hazardous Substances
- schedule: OTC — unrestricted purchase

- risks: DELIRIANT — not a fun hallucinogen: users can't distinguish hallucination from reality; Heart arrhythmia — anticholinergic load strains the heart; deaths documented; Seizures; Urinary retention, hyperthermia; The 'Benadryl challenge' on TikTok sent teens to the ER — and killed some; Extremely uncomfortable — most users never repeat it
- overdoseSigns: Delirium, confusion, hallucinations; Racing irregular heartbeat; Seizures; Urinary retention, flushed skin, dilated pupils
- streetPrice: $3–$8 per box (OTC) — pocket-money dangerous
- legalStatus: OTC unrestricted — the accessibility is the danger

## Botulinum Toxin (Botox)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/botox/
- aliases: Botox, BTX-A, Anti-wrinkle injections, Baby Botox
- category: Beauty Industry & Med Spa
- schedule: Rx-only biologic (US/EU); unregulated cosmetic market enormous
- appearance: Clear vials of freeze-dried toxin, reconstituted with saline; injected in units
- effects: Paralyzes injected muscles — smooths wrinkles for 3–4 months; Medical uses: migraines, excessive sweating, muscle spasms
- risks: BLACK-MARKET BOTOX: counterfeit vials, overdosed units, and fake 'Botox parties' cause drooping, asymmetry, swallowing/breathing difficulty; Injection into wrong muscle: eyelid ptosis (drooping eye), uneven smile — lasts weeks-months; Brow/eyelid heaviness from poor placement; Vascular occlusion — filler injected into artery = skin death; blindness is documented from forehead/nose injections; Teen trend: 'baby Botox' and preventative injections at 18–25 with zero long-term data; Unlicensed injectors — no medical training, no emergency supplies, no hyaluronidase to dissolve mistakes
- overdoseSigns: Difficulty swallowing or breathing (toxin spread); Muscle weakness spreading beyond injection site; Vision changes (if near eye)
- streetPrice: Legit: $10–$15 per unit (forehead = 20–40 units = $200–$600); black-market parties $50–$150
- legalStatus: Rx-only biologic; must be administered by licensed medical professionals; black-market parties illegal in most places
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: FDA, EMA, ASPS

## Dermal Fillers (HA & Biostimulators)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/dermal-fillers/
- aliases: Lip filler, Juvederm, Restylane, Cheek filler, Dermal filler
- category: Beauty Industry & Med Spa
- schedule: Rx-only devices (US) — unregulated market huge
- appearance: Syringes/pre-filled pens of hyaluronic acid gel (Juvederm, Restylane) or biostimulators (Sculptra); or black-market filler vials sold online
- effects: Adds volume: lips, cheeks, jawline, under-eyes; HA fillers reversible with hyaluronidase
- risks: VASCULAR OCCLUSION — the big one: filler injected into an artery blocks blood flow → skin necrosis (black dying skin) or BLINDNESS (filler migrating to eye artery; ~300+ documented cases); Unlicensed injector + no hyaluronidase on hand = occlusion becomes catastrophe; Vascular occlusion happens to licensed injectors too — emergency protocol knowledge is the difference; Black-market filler: industrial-grade silicone, cooking oil, and non-medical HA cause granulomas, migration, disfigurement; Teen epidemic: lip filler at 16–20 normalized on TikTok; long-term effects unknown; Filler fatigue — repeated overfilling stretches tissue
- overdoseSigns: Blanching/white skin at injection site (occlusion sign); Severe pain during/after injection; Vision changes or loss — EMERGENCY; Skin turning black (necrosis)
- streetPrice: Legit: $500–$2,000 per syringe; black-market kits $30–$150 online; kitchen-table parties $100–$300
- legalStatus: Rx-only medical devices; must be administered by licensed professionals; DIY kits and parties are unregulated/illegal
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: FDA, EMA, ASPS

## Black-Market Silicone Injections
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/silicone-injections/
- aliases: Pumping parties, Butt shots, Biopolymer injections, Industrial silicone
- category: Beauty Industry & Med Spa
- schedule: Illegal for body contouring (US) — FDA black-box warning
- appearance: Industrial silicone oil or biopolymer gel injected at 'pumping parties' — hips, buttocks, breasts, lips
- effects: Permanent volume — the reason people risk it
- risks: BODY HORROR: industrial-grade (not medical) silicone causes granulomas, chronic inflammation, silicone migration to lungs/kidneys; Multiple documented DEATHS from embolism (silicone entering bloodstream); Deformed, hardened tissue — 'cement butt'; Removal requires massive reconstructive surgery — often impossible to fully remove; No licensed practitioner will do it — only unlicensed injectors at parties; Popularized in trans communities and body-mod scenes with tragic outcomes
- overdoseSigns: Difficulty breathing (silicone embolism to lungs); Chest pain, coughing blood; Fever, severe pain at injection site; Silicone migration lumps
- streetPrice: $500–$2,000 per 'session' at pumping parties
- legalStatus: Illegal — FDA black-box warning; deaths prosecuted as manslaughter/murder in multiple US cases
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17

## Hyaluronidase (Filler Dissolver)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/hyaluronidase/
- aliases: Hyalase, Vitrase, Hylenex, Filler eraser
- category: Beauty Industry & Med Spa
- schedule: Rx-only enzyme
- appearance: Vials of enzyme powder, reconstituted to inject
- effects: Dissolves hyaluronic-acid filler within hours — the 'undo button' for HA fillers; Spreads injected drugs (historical medical use)
- risks: Allergic reactions including anaphylaxis — must be available at any filler appointment; Over-dissolution: removes your OWN hyaluronic acid — temporary hollowing/deflation; Does NOT work on biostimulators (Sculptra) or silicone — irreversible fillers have no undo; Black-market injectors don't stock it — occlusion without hyaluronidase = necrosis/blindness
- overdoseSigns: Allergic reaction: hives, swelling, difficulty breathing; Excessive tissue dissolution
- streetPrice: $50–$150 per vial (clinic cost)
- legalStatus: Rx-only; the reason any legitimate filler clinic must have a licensed prescriber present
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: FDA, EMA

## Carfentanil
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/carfentanil/
- aliases: Wildnil, Elephant tranquilizer
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US) — veterinary only; analogues prosecuted
- appearance: White powder — 100× fentanyl, dosed in MICROGRAMS; occasionally found in heroin/fentanyl supplies
- effects: Fentanyl-family opioid sedation — intended for large-animal anesthesia ONLY
- risks: 10,000× morphine potency — 1–2 mg (a few granules) can be fatal to humans; Found mixed into street heroin/cocaine — mass-overdose clusters; Skin absorption risk — handling powder can poison responders; Naloxone works but MASSIVE/REPEATED doses needed (10+ sprays); No human medical use exists
- overdoseSigns: Instant respiratory arrest; Pinpoint pupils; Cyanosis (blue/gray skin); Death within minutes
- streetPrice: N/A — mass-casualty contaminant; found in seized street supplies
- legalStatus: Schedule II veterinary only; human possession = felony; analogue prosecutions automatic
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: DEA, NIDA

## Amanita Muscaria (Fly Agaric Mushrooms)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/amanita-muscaria/
- aliases: Fly agaric, Mario mushroom, Amanita, Muscimol mushrooms
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Unregulated (US federal); legal most places
- appearance: Red-capped mushroom with white spots — the Mario mushroom; sold dried, in gummies, or extracts
- effects: Muscimol (not psilocybin): sedating, dreamlike, deliriant — unlike classic psychedelics; Giggling, drowsiness, vivid dreams
- risks: NOT psilocybin — ibotenic acid causes confusion, agitation, vomiting; Preparation matters: improper drying leaves toxic ibotenic acid (neurotoxic); Lookalike DEATH CAP risk — Amanita phalloides kills; misidentification is fatal; Unregulated gummies/extracts — dosing unknown; Sedation + vomiting = aspiration risk; TikTok 'legal mushroom' trend — teens buying without research

- streetPrice: ~$10–$30 dried caps; gummies $20–$40; extracts $25–$60
- legalStatus: Unregulated federal US; legal most states/countries (Louisiana restricted); 'legal high' marketing
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, Poison Control

- effects: Methamphetamine + caffeine combination: intense euphoria, energy, alertness; Smoked on foil ('chasing the dragon' style)
- risks: Methamphetamine harms: addiction, psychosis, cardiovascular damage; Southeast Asia epidemic — Thailand's 'crazy medicine'; Insomnia, paranoia, aggression with heavy use; Cut with ketamine or heroin in some batches
- overdoseSigns: Racing heart, chest pain; Extreme agitation, paranoia; Hyperthermia, seizures
- streetPrice: $1–$5 per pill (SEA); smuggled to West at higher prices
- legalStatus: Illegal everywhere; Southeast Asia's signature meth problem
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: UNODC, NIDA

## Khat (Catha edulis)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/khat/

- category: Stimulants
- schedule: Schedule I (US); legal some countries (UK until 2014, Yemen, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia)
- appearance: Fresh green leaves chewed in sessions; must be fresh — dries out and loses potency
- effects: Mild stimulant: alertness, euphoria, talkativeness; Appetite suppression, insomnia
- risks: Academic/work decline — daily chewing sessions consume hours; Dependence with daily use; Cardiovascular strain; rare heart attacks; Constipation, gastric issues; Social harm in producing countries — economic burden, water depletion

- streetPrice: $5–$20 per bundle where legal; $50+ smuggled fresh to diaspora markets

## Betel Quid (Areca Nut / Paan)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/betel-quid/
- aliases: Paan, Betel nut, Areca nut, Supari, Gutka
- category: Hazardous Substances
- schedule: Legal most places; regulated India/Pakistan; IARC Group 1 carcinogen
- appearance: Areca nut wrapped in betel leaf with slaked lime (+ tobacco sometimes); chewed and spat or swallowed
- effects: Mild stimulant: alertness, warmth, euphoria at first chew; Red saliva, stained teeth
- risks: GROUP 1 CARCINOGEN — oral cancer risk comparable to tobacco; red-stained oral lesions precede cancer; 400M+ users in South/Southeast Asia — massive public health burden; Recreational use among youth in diaspora communities; TMJ damage, tooth destruction; Addictive — arecoline is psychoactive
- overdoseSigns: Oral lesions, white/red patches (precancerous); Difficulty opening mouth (oral submucous fibrosis); Jaw pain
- streetPrice: $0.10–$1 per quid — pennies-scale addiction
- legalStatus: Legal most places; India/Pakistan regulate packaged gutka; IARC Group 1 confirmed carcinogen
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: WHO, IARC, EMCDDA

## Krokodil (Desomorphine)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/krokodil/
- aliases: Krokodil, Crocodile, Russian magic
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule I (US analogues); controlled worldwide
- appearance: Homemade injectable from codeine pills + gasoline + iodine + red phosphorus — dirty amber liquid
- effects: Short, powerful opioid high (8–10× morphine, shorter than heroin)
- risks: THE FLESH-EATING DRUG — impurities (phosphorus, gasoline residue) destroy tissue at injection sites: black scaly skin (hence 'crocodile'), rotting flesh, exposed bone; Gangrene, amputations, organ damage; Russia's 2010s epidemic — thousands of users with horrendous wounds; Life expectancy after addiction onset: 2–3 years; DIY synthesis = poison injected directly
- overdoseSigns: Respiratory depression; Rotting injection sites, black skin; Sepsis, organ failure
- streetPrice: Homemade — ~cost of codeine pills + solvents ($5–$20 per batch)
- legalStatus: Illegal everywhere; desomorphine analogues prosecuted
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: EMCDDA, NIDA, WHO

- appearance: Pills/powder — sold with BZP as 'legal ecstasy'
- effects: Mild MDMA-like stimulation/euphoria; Serotonin release
- risks: Sold as 'legal X' — the piperazine epidemic of the 2000s; Serotonin syndrome risk with real MDMA or antidepressants; Headaches, nausea; Seizures documented
- overdoseSigns: Serotonin syndrome; Seizures; Severe headache, nausea
- streetPrice: ~$5–$15 per pill (residual)
- legalStatus: Analogue US; controlled EU/CA/AU
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: EMCDDA, NIDA

## Rick Simpson Oil (RSO / Phoenix Tears)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/cannabis-oil-rso/
- aliases: RSO, Phoenix Tears, Cannabis oil, FECO
- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Follows local cannabis law; unregulated where illegal
- appearance: Dark black/brown thick cannabis extract; sold in syringes
- effects: Heavy sedating high — full-spectrum THC extract; Cancer-patient community use
- risks: CANCER-CURE CLAIMS — RSO is marketed as a cancer cure with zero evidence; patients delay real treatment and die; Extremely potent — rice-grain doses for novices; Made with naphtha/isopropyl — residual solvents if poorly purged; Unregulated dosing = overconsumption; No quality control in grey market
- overdoseSigns: Severe sedation; Anxiety, paranoia; Vomiting
- streetPrice: $30–$60 per gram (grey); dispensary extracts vary
- legalStatus: Follows cannabis law; 'cancer cure' marketing is health fraud
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: FDA, NIDA, Cancer Research UK

## Dabs / Shatter / Wax (THC Concentrates)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/dabs-shatter/
- aliases: Dabs, Shatter, Wax, BHO, Live resin, Rosin,  crumble
- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Follows cannabis law; concentrates felony in some prohibition states
- appearance: Amber glass-like shatter, waxy crumble, sticky live resin; vaporized on hot nails
- effects: Instant intense high — 60–90% THC vs 15–25% flower; Dabbing delivers massive single hits
- risks: TOLERANCE EXPLOSION — daily dabbing requires gram-level tolerance in months; Psychosis risk at 90% THC — documented in heavy concentrate users; BHO extraction explosions — home hash-oil labs burn down; Residual solvents in poorly-purged BHO; Cannabis hyperemesis — uncontrollable vomiting in heavy users; Youth 'dabbing' trend — the strongest entry to cannabis
- overdoseSigns: Cannabinoid hyperemesis (cyclical vomiting); Severe anxiety, paranoia; Fainting
- streetPrice: $20–$60/g dispensary; $30–$80/g grey
- legalStatus: Follows cannabis law; home BHO production illegal most places (explosion hazard)
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: NIDA, CDC

## CBD Flower / Hemp Bud
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/cbd-flower/
- aliases: CBD bud, Hemp flower, CBD weed
- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Federally legal US (<0.3% Delta-9 THC); state patchwork
- appearance: Looks/smells identical to cannabis flower — legal-sale grey zone
- effects: Relaxation without strong high (if truly low-THC); Some products carry real THC anyway
- risks: LOOKALIKE PROBLEM — indistinguishable from illegal cannabis by sight/smell; police can't tell, users misdose; Products testing ABOVE 0.3% THC — legal felony in prohibition states; Contamination: heavy metals, pesticides in unregulated hemp; 'Legal weed' marketing confuses users and law enforcement
- overdoseSigns: Unexpected high if THC-laden; Anxiety if sensitive
- streetPrice: $5–$15/g flower; prerolls $3–$10
- legalStatus: Federally legal (Farm Bill); state bans/patchwork; testing disputes ongoing
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: FDA, NIDA

## THC-P (Tetrahydrocannabiphorol)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/thcp/
- aliases: THC-P, THCP
- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Federally unscheduled; DEA gray; banned several states
- appearance: Vapes, gummies — semi-synthetic 'super THC'
- effects: 33× CB1 affinity vs THC — extremely potent high; Long duration (8–12 h)
- risks: Potency makes overdose (anxiety, psychosis) likely for novices; Semi-synthetic — no human safety data; Unregulated products; Detectable on drug tests for weeks
- overdoseSigns: Severe anxiety, paranoia; Prolonged impairment; Psychosis risk
- streetPrice: $25–$60 vapes; gummies $20–$50
- legalStatus: Federally unscheduled (hemp-derived); banned some states; DEA watching
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: FDA, NIDA

## Cigarettes
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/cigarettes/
- aliases: Cigs, Smokes, Fags, Cancer sticks, Squares
- category: Tobacco & Nicotine
- schedule: Legal 18/21+ worldwide; advertising heavily restricted
- appearance: White filtered sticks or unfiltered; packs with graphic warnings in most countries
- effects: Nicotine hit in 10 seconds: alertness, calm, appetite suppression; The ritual: hand-to-mouth, smoke breaks, social bonding
- risks: THE leading preventable cause of death — 8 million deaths/year globally, ~480,000/year US; Half of long-term smokers die from it: lung cancer, COPD, heart disease, stroke; Every cigarette shortens life ~11 minutes; a pack a day = 7 years over a lifetime; Adolescent nicotine rewires the developing brain — attention, mood, impulse control; Not just lungs: bladder, pancreas, cervix, colorectal cancers; Secondhand smoke kills ~1.2 million non-smokers/year
- overdoseSigns: Nicotine poisoning (rare from smoking alone): nausea, dizziness, vomiting; Racing heart, sweating; Severe poisoning (kids eating cigarettes/vapes): seizures, respiratory failure — emergency
- streetPrice: $5–$15 per pack (US; $15–30 NYC/AU); cheapest drug addiction per day
- legalStatus: Legal adult product; sale to minors banned everywhere; plain packaging in UK/AU/France
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: WHO, CDC, NIDA

## Nicotine E-Cigarettes & Disposables
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/nicotine-vapes/
- aliases: Vapes, E-cigs, Elf Bar, Esco Bar, Puff Bar, JUUL
- category: Tobacco & Nicotine
- schedule: Legal 18/21+; FDA authorization required (most disposables unapproved)
- appearance: Colorful disposables (Elf Bar, Esco Bar), pod systems, mods; candy/fruit flavors
- effects: Fast nicotine: the same 10-second brain hit as cigarettes; Smooth high-nicotine salts — easy to inhale deeply, easy to overuse
- risks: THE teen nicotine epidemic — 2023-2025: disposables with up to 5% (50 mg/mL) nicotine salt, designed for addiction; Adolescent brain development disruption — attention, learning, mood regulation, impulse control; One disposable = a pack+ of cigarettes in nicotine; EVALI-style lung injuries tied to black-market THC carts; nicotine vapes carry their own unknowns; Gateway pattern: teens who vape are 3–4× more likely to start smoking; Battery explosions, nicotine poisoning in toddlers who eat pods
- overdoseSigns: Nicotine poisoning: nausea, vomiting, dizziness, sweating; Racing heart, tremor; Severe: seizures, respiratory distress — emergency (especially children)
- streetPrice: $5–$25 per disposable (400–6000 puffs); pods $10–$20
- legalStatus: Legal adult product; flavors restricted/banned US, EU, UK; disposable bans spreading (UK 2025)
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: CDC, FDA, WHO

## Snus (Swedish Oral Tobacco)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/snus/
- aliases: Snus, Swedish snus, Nicotine pouches (tobacco version)
- category: Tobacco & Nicotine
- schedule: Legal Sweden (EU exemption); illegal to sell elsewhere EU; legal US 21+
- appearance: Small teabag-like pouches placed under the lip; loose moist tobacco versions
- effects: Steady nicotine release 30–60 min: alertness, calm; No smoke, no spitting
- risks: THE HARM-REDUCTION DEBATE: Swedish snus is proven far safer than smoking — Sweden has Europe's lowest male lung-cancer rates — but it is NOT harmless; Oral cancer risk (lower than chewing tobacco, not zero); Nicotine addiction identical to smoking; Gum recession, tooth staining, mouth lesions; Pregnancy risks (nicotine restricts fetal blood flow)
- overdoseSigns: Nicotine poisoning at high doses: nausea, dizziness; Sleep disruption, palpitations
- streetPrice: $4–$8 per can (24 portions) Sweden; $7–$15 US imports
- legalStatus: Legal Sweden; banned elsewhere EU (sales); legal US 21+ as modified-risk tobacco product
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: WHO, CDC, EMCDDA

## Chewing Tobacco & Dip
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/chewing-tobacco/
- aliases: Chew, Dip, Snuff, Plug, Spit tobacco
- category: Tobacco & Nicotine
- schedule: Legal 18/21+ US; banned EU sales
- appearance: Loose leaf, plug, or fine-cut moist snuff placed in the lip/cheek; spit cup culture
- effects: Steady nicotine via oral mucosa; spittoon ritual; Stronger nicotine dose than cigarettes per session
- risks: ORAL CANCER — the signature harm: cheek, gum, tongue cancers; often diagnosed late; Leukoplakia (white precancerous mouth patches) in most heavy users; Tooth loss, gum destruction, jaw bone loss; Esophageal and pancreatic cancers; Nicotine addiction equal to smoking; Baseball/country culture normalizes it for teens
- overdoseSigns: Nicotine poisoning: nausea, dizziness, sweating; Heart palpitations
- streetPrice: $4–$8 per can
- legalStatus: Legal US 21+; EU sales ban (Sweden snus exempt)
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: CDC, WHO, NCI

## Hookah / Shisha
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/hookah-shisha/
- aliases: Shisha, Waterpipe, Nargile, Hubbly bubbly
- category: Tobacco & Nicotine
- schedule: Legal 18+ in licensed venues (varies); home use legal
- appearance: Waterpipe with flavored tobacco (apple, mint, grape); charcoal-heated; group sessions 30–90 min
- effects: Social, relaxing 30–90 min sessions; flavored smooth smoke; Head buzz from nicotine + charcoal CO
- risks: THE 'SAFE' MYTH — water does NOT filter toxins. A 1-hour session = 100–200 cigarettes' smoke volume; High CO (carbon monoxide) from charcoal — headaches, fainting; dangerous in pregnancy; Same cancer and heart risks as cigarettes, multiplied by session length; Infectious sharing: TB, herpes, hepatitis via shared mouthpieces; Youth social normalization — shisha cafes near universities; Secondhand smoke harms everyone in the venue
- overdoseSigns: Carbon monoxide poisoning: headache, dizziness, nausea, fainting; Nicotine poisoning in novices
- streetPrice: $10–$25 per venue session; home pipes $30–$150; shisha $10–$30/250g
- legalStatus: Legal adult venues; indoor-smoking laws apply; some cities ban flavored shisha
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: WHO, CDC, EMCDDA

## Cigars & Cigarillos
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/cigars/
- aliases: Cigars, Cigarillos, Backwoods, Swisher Sweets, Blunts
- category: Tobacco & Nicotine
- schedule: Legal 18/21+; taxed lower than cigarettes in US (loophole)
- appearance: Large cigars, small cigarillos (Backwoods, Swishers); the #1 wrap for blunts
- effects: Nicotine — cigars can contain 5–20× a cigarette's nicotine; absorbed through mouth lining even without inhaling
- risks: Cigar smoking causes the same cancers as cigarettes — lung, oral, esophageal, laryngeal — even if you don't inhale; Single cigars can deliver a pack's nicotine; THE BLUNT WRAP PIPELINE — cigarillos exist in youth cannabis culture as blunt wraps; sweet flavors (wine, strawberry) marketed at young buyers; Secondhand cigar smoke more toxic than cigarette smoke; Lower taxes = cheaper entry point for teens
- overdoseSigns: Nicotine poisoning: nausea, dizziness; Palpitations
- streetPrice: $1–$5 per cigarillo; $5–$30 premium cigars
- legalStatus: Legal adult; flavor ban debates ongoing; blunt-wrap marketing criticized
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: CDC, NCI, FDA

## Bidis & Kreteks (Clove Cigarettes)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/bidis-kreteks/
- aliases: Bidis, Beedis, Kreteks, Clove cigs
- category: Tobacco & Nicotine
- schedule: Kreteks banned US (flavored cig ban, 2009); bidis restricted; legal some countries
- appearance: Bidis: hand-rolled tobacco in tendu leaf, tied with string. Kreteks: clove-spiced cigarettes
- effects: Nicotine plus clove's numbing eugenol — smoke feels smooth, deeper inhaled; Crackling sensation from cloves
- risks: Bidis: unregulated hand-rolling = higher tar and nicotine than cigarettes; made by child labor in India; Kreteks: eugenol numbs the throat → deeper inhalation → more damage; banned as flavored cigarettes in US (still sold as 'cigars'); Same cancer/COPD/cardiac risk profile as cigarettes; Cheap price point = youth entry product
- overdoseSigns: Nicotine poisoning; CO-related headache/dizziness
- streetPrice: $2–$5 per pack bidis; kreteks $3–$6
- legalStatus: Kreteks banned as cigarettes US (sold as filtered cigars); bidis face import restrictions
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: CDC, WHO, FDA

## Nicotine Replacement (Gum, Patch, Lozenge)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/nicotine-replacement/
- aliases: NRT, Nicorette, Nicotine patch, Quit smoking aids
- category: Tobacco & Nicotine
- schedule: OTC (US/EU) — no prescription needed
- appearance: Gum (2/4 mg), transdermal patches (7–21 mg), lozenges, sprays, inhalers (Rx some places)
- effects: Steady controlled nicotine — kills cravings and withdrawal without smoke; The most-proven quit-smoking tool: doubles quit success
- risks: FAR safer than smoking — the harm comes from combustion, not nicotine; Possible side effects: vivid dreams (patch), hiccups/jaw ache (gum), skin irritation; Dependency on NRT possible but rare and far less harmful than smoking; NOT for non-smokers — adolescent nicotine use in any form is harmful; Combining patch + gum is standard clinical practice for heavy smokers
- overdoseSigns: Overuse: nausea, dizziness, racing heart (rare; lower risk than smoking overdose); Proper use: virtually no overdose risk
- streetPrice: $25–$50 per 2-week supply; free through many quitlines (1-800-QUIT-NOW US)
- legalStatus: OTC; free/covered in many national health systems as cessation therapy
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-17
- sources: CDC, NICE, WHO

## Alcohol (Ethanol)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/alcohol/
- aliases: Booze, Liquor, Spirits, Beer, Wine, Ethanol
- category: GHB / GBL
- schedule: Legal adult product worldwide; sale to minors banned
- appearance: Beer, wine, spirits; 5-40% ABV; also hand sanitizer and mouthwash when desperate
- effects: Euphoria, disinhibition, social ease at low doses; Sedation, impaired coordination, slurred speech; Dopamine release in the reward pathway
- risks: THE most harmful drug in most countries by total harm scores: liver disease (cirrhosis), cancer (7 types — breast, colon, liver...); Dependence: ~10-15% of regular heavy drinkers; withdrawal can KILL (seizures, delirium tremens — deadlier than heroin withdrawal); Binge drinking: alcohol poisoning stops breathing; choking on vomit while unconscious; Brain damage, hypertension, cardiomyopathy, pancreatitis; Fetal alcohol syndrome — no safe dose in pregnancy; Mixing with benzos, GHB, opioids, or sleeping pills multiplies respiratory depression
- overdoseSigns: Vomiting while semi-conscious; Slow/irregular breathing (<8/min); Cold clammy skin, bluish lips; Cannot be woken (passing out is not sleep)
- streetPrice: ~$1–$3 per standard drink retail; the cheapest drug per unit of effect
- legalStatus: Legal 18/21+ globally; Prohibition nowhere comprehensive; Muslim-majority countries ban or heavily restrict
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: WHO, NIDA, CDC

## 1,4-Butanediol (1,4-BDO)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/1-4-bdo/
- aliases: BDO, 1,4-B, One Four, Gold cleaner, Thunder Nectar
- category: GHB / GBL
- schedule: Not federally scheduled US (analogue prosecutions possible); industrial chemical regulations EU
- appearance: Clear, odorless-to-sweet viscous liquid; sold as 'cleaner', 'extract', or industrial solvent
- effects: Converts to GHB in the body — identical effects: euphoria, disinhibition, sedation; Onset slower than GHB (30-60 min)
- risks: GHB-class dangers: razor-thin overdose margin — 1 mL too much = coma; Severe daily-use dependence with life-threatening withdrawal (like GHB/alcohol); Industrial-grade supply = unknown purity/concentration; Frequently mislabeled or mixed with GBL; Emergency: no field antidote — airway support only
- overdoseSigns: Sudden deep sleep/unrousable; Vomiting while unconscious; Slow irregular breathing
- streetPrice: ~$40–$100 per 100 mL industrial; 'cleaner' branding $30–$80
- legalStatus: Unscheduled federally US but prosecuted as GHB analogue; EU REACH industrial restrictions; human consumption not legal anywhere
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: EMCDDA, NIDA, DEA

## Methaqualone (Quaalude / Mandrax)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/methaqualone/
- aliases: Quaalude, Ludes, Mandrax, Mandies, Disco biscuits
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Schedule I (US, since 1984); controlled worldwide
- appearance: White tablets (historical 'Lemmon 714'); modern mandrax = crushed methaqualone mixed with cannabis smoked in SA pipes
- effects: Sedative-hypnotic: relaxation, euphoria, disinhibition, legendary 'aphrodisiac' myth; At higher doses: stumbling 'luding out'
- risks: The original party pill of the 1970s — banned after dependence and overdose epidemics; Respiratory depression, seizures in overdose; South Africa's mandrax epidemic continues — smoked with cannabis ('white pipe'); Modern black-market 'ludes' are almost always fake (benzos, diphenhydramine); Withdrawal: seizures, hallucinations
- overdoseSigns: Deep coma; Slow/absent breathing; Seizures; Pinpoint-then-dilated pupils
- streetPrice: Fake tablets $5–$20; real mandrax $2–$10 per tablet in SA
- legalStatus: Schedule I US; illegal everywhere; South Africa's most-abused sedative despite bans
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, DEA

## Temazepam (Restoril / Normison)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/temazepam/
- aliases: Restoril, Normison, Euhypnos, Jellies, Eggs
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule IV (US); Class C (UK)
- appearance: Gelatin capsules 7.5–30 mg (the famous UK 'yellow/blue eggs'); tablets
- effects: Hypnotic: sleep induction within 30 min; Anxiolysis, muscle relaxation
- risks: THE injecting benzo: UK's 1990s 'jellies' epidemic — temazepam gel injected, causing limb ischemia, gangrene, amputations; Dependence within 2-4 weeks; brutal withdrawal (seizures); Hanging-over impairment: falls, driving deaths in older users; Mixing with opioids/alcohol: respiratory depression
- overdoseSigns: Deep sedation; Slow breathing with other depressants; Slurred speech, ataxia
- streetPrice: ~$1–$5 per capsule diverted; historically the most-injected UK benzo
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule IV; gel capsule formulation withdrawn in some markets over injection harms
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: NHS, EMCDDA, FDA

## Chlordiazepoxide (Librium)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/chlordiazepoxide/
- aliases: Librium, CDX, Libritabs
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule IV (US)
- appearance: 5–25 mg capsules/tablets, green/white/yellow
- effects: Long-acting calm, anxiety relief, alcohol-withdrawal control; The original benzodiazepine (1960)
- risks: Same class dependence and withdrawal-seizure risk; Long half-life = accumulation in elderly, falls; The standard alcohol-detox medication — diverted for self-detoxing, which without monitoring can still seize; Often given out too freely in South Asia
- overdoseSigns: Sedation; Confusion; Slow breathing in combination
- streetPrice: ~$0.50–$2 per capsule grey-market
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule IV; first-line for alcohol withdrawal in most protocols
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, NHS

## Oxazepam (Serax)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/oxazepam/
- aliases: Serax, Serepax, Alepam
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule IV (US)
- appearance: 10–30 mg tablets/capsules
- effects: Intermediate-acting anxiolytic, less sedating than diazepam; No active metabolites — safer in liver disease
- risks: Still dependence-forming with daily use; Less potent per mg — users underestimate doses; Withdrawal seizures after long use; Alcohol interaction
- overdoseSigns: Sedation; Dizziness; Slow breathing in combination
- streetPrice: ~$0.50–$2 per tablet
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule IV
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, EMCDDA

## Midazolam (Versed / Dormicum)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/midazolam/
- aliases: Versed, Dormicum, Midaz, The execution drug
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule IV (US); hospital-only in most countries
- appearance: Clear injectable ampoules (1–5 mg/mL); oral syrup; rarely diverted tablets
- effects: Ultra-short IV sedation, anterograde amnesia — the procedural-sedation workhorse; Rapid, powerful
- risks: IV use by non-medical people: respiratory arrest — narrow margin, no reversal at home; Amnesia makes dosing errors lethal (users redose forgetting they dosed); Used in lethal-injection protocols and US executions; Diverted ampoules linked to overdose deaths
- overdoseSigns: Respiratory arrest; Unconsciousness with slow breathing; Flaccid paralysis of breathing effort
- streetPrice: Diverted ampoules $10–$40 each
- legalStatus: Rx/hospital-only, Schedule IV; IV administration restricted to monitored settings
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, EMA, NIDA

## Clobazam (Onfi / Frisium)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/clobazam/
- aliases: Onfi, Frisium, Urbanol, Castilium
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Schedule IV (US); Class C (UK)
- appearance: 10–20 mg tablets, white scored
- effects: Calm with less sedation than classic benzos — a 1,5-benzodiazepine; Epilepsy and anxiety indications
- risks: Dependence still real despite 'gentler' reputation; Withdrawal seizures — especially dangerous in epilepsy patients who stop abruptly; Overdose with opioids; Accumulation with long half-life (~36h)
- overdoseSigns: Sedation; Respiratory depression in combination; Dizziness
- streetPrice: ~$0.50–$2 per tablet grey-market
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule IV
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, EMA

## Norflurazepam
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/norflurazepam/
- aliases: N-Desalkylflurazepam, Norflura
- category: Benzodiazepines
- schedule: Analogue prosecutions (US); controlled several EU states
- appearance: White/off-white powder or pellets; active metabolite of flurazepam sold as RC
- effects: Long-acting benzo sedation and calm; Active 40–250 h — days-long effects
- risks: Extreme duration: dosing daily creates compounding blood levels for weeks; Blackouts, falls, car crashes at functional doses; Withdrawal protracted and seizure-prone; Found in fake 'diazepam' tablets (alongside etizolam, flubromazepam)
- overdoseSigns: Days-long sedation; Impaired driving without feeling impaired; Respiratory depression in combination
- streetPrice: ~$1–$4 per pellet equivalent
- legalStatus: Analogue Act (US); scheduled DE/UK/NL and spreading
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: EMCDDA, NPS-AD, TripSit

## Zaleplon (Sonata)

- aliases: Sonata, Starnoc
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Schedule IV (US)
- appearance: 5–20 mg capsules, green/white
- effects: Ultra-short hypnotic — sleep within 15 min, ~4 h duration; Less hangover than zolpidem for some
- risks: Same Z-drug dependence class; Sleep-driving/walking documented; Middle-of-the-night redosing = accumulation crashes; Counterfeits in grey market

## Meprobamate (Miltown)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/meprobamate/
- aliases: Miltown, Equanil, Meprospan, Meprotabs
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Schedule IV (US, since 1970)
- appearance: 200–600 mg tablets, white
- effects: 1950s 'happiness pill': calm, muscle relaxation, mild euphoria; Still the active metabolite of carisoprodol (Soma)
- risks: The original mass-market tranquilizer dependence scandal (1950s-60s); Overdose: respiratory depression, coma, hypotension; Withdrawal: seizures, hallucinations; Carisoprodol users get meprobamate exposure — double dependency pathway
- overdoseSigns: Sedation then coma; Low blood pressure; Slow breathing
- streetPrice: Rare; $0.50–$2 grey-market where diverted
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule IV US; controlled most regions; legacy drug
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, NIDA

## Gabapentin (Neurontin)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/gabapentin/
- aliases: Neurontin, Gabbies, Johnnies, Gapentin
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Not federally scheduled US (state controls in ~15 states); POM UK/EU/AU
- appearance: 100–800 mg capsules/tablets
- effects: Calm, sedation at high doses; nerve-pain relief at prescribed doses; Recreational doses (1–3 g+) produce a floaty opioid-ish calm
- risks: THE pregabalin shadow: same class, same misuse — present in a large share of opioid-overdose toxicologies; Mixing with opioids multiplies respiratory depression — this combination kills; Dependence and a nasty withdrawal (anxiety, insomnia, nausea); Diverted heavily in prisons and opioid-using communities
- overdoseSigns: Extreme sedation; Slurred speech, ataxia; Respiratory depression (especially with opioids)
- streetPrice: ~$0.50–$2 per 800 mg capsule grey-market
- legalStatus: Rx-only; US states increasingly scheduling (Schedule V in ~15); UK reclassified POM 2019
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, NHS, EMCDDA

## Quetiapine (Seroquel)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/quetiapine/
- aliases: Seroquel, Suzie Q, Q-ball, Squirt
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Rx-only — not a controlled drug
- appearance: 25–400 mg tablets, peach/white
- effects: Heavy sedation, 'turning off' — not euphoric, users chase the off-switch; Prescribed for schizophrenia, bipolar, off-label insomnia
- risks: The prison/street sleep drug: 'Suzie Q' trades as currency — it's numbing, not a high; Metabolic harm: weight gain, diabetes, dyslipidemia even at low doses; QT prolongation; sudden cardiac death risk in overdose; Withdrawal insomnia rebound drives compulsive redosing; Combined with opioids: additive respiratory depression
- overdoseSigns: Extreme sedation, unrousable; Racing then irregular heart; Low blood pressure
- streetPrice: ~$0.50–$3 per tablet; high prison currency value
- legalStatus: Rx-only; one of the most-diverted non-controlled drugs in the US/UK
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, EMA, NIDA

## Mirtazapine (Remeron)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/mirtazapine/
- aliases: Remeron, Mirtaz, Zispin
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Rx-only — not controlled
- appearance: 15–45 mg tablets (orodispersible 'sol-tabs' exist)
- effects: Sedation and appetite increase at low doses; antidepressant at 30–45 mg; Popular off-label sleep aid
- risks: Not euphoric but dependence-forming as a sleep crutch; Weight gain, intense hunger (some abuse for appetite); Withdrawal: nausea, insomnia, anxiety, 'electric shocks'; Serotonin syndrome risk combined with other serotonergic drugs; Morning impairment: driving, falls
- overdoseSigns: Severe sedation; Confusion; Heart rhythm changes (rare)
- streetPrice: ~$0.30–$1 per tablet grey-market
- legalStatus: Rx-only everywhere; widely prescribed, often loose follow-up
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, EMA, NHS

## Trazodone (Desyrel)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/trazodone/
- aliases: Desyrel, Traz, Oleptro
- category: Sedatives & Hypnotics
- schedule: Rx-only — not controlled
- appearance: 50–300 mg tablets, white scored
- effects: Sedating antidepressant — the classic off-label sleep prescription; Antianxiety at low doses
- risks: PRIAPISM — the famous side effect: painful erections lasting hours; untreated = permanent damage. Emergency if >4 h; Orthostatic hypotension: falls, dizziness; Serotonin syndrome in combination; Dependence as a sleep crutch; withdrawal insomnia
- overdoseSigns: Priapism (emergency); Severe dizziness, fainting; Irregular heart rhythm
- streetPrice: ~$0.20–$1 per tablet
- legalStatus: Rx-only; among the most-prescribed sleep meds in the US
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, NHS

## Tramadol (Ultram)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/tramadol/
- aliases: Ultram, Tramal, Trammies, Chill pills, Ultracet (with APAP)
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule IV (US); POM most places; heavily consumed Africa/Middle East/Asia
- appearance: 50–100 mg tablets/capsules; 50 mg/ml drops; IV ampoules
- effects: Weak opioid pain relief plus SNRI effects: warmth, mood lift, energy at recreational doses; Seizure risk is dose-dependent
- risks: SEIZURES — tramadol lowers the seizure threshold; doses above 400 mg/day or combos (SSRIs, stimulants, antipsychotics) can trigger them; Serotonin syndrome with antidepressants or MDMA; Dependence and withdrawal (SNRI + opioid double withdrawal: brain zaps + flu); Africa's and the Middle East's most-abused opioid — Egypt, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia epidemics; CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizers convert it to O-DSMT fast — accidental overdose
- overdoseSigns: Seizures; Pinpoint pupils with respiratory depression; Serotonin-syndrome signs: agitation, clonus, fever
- streetPrice: ~$0.10–$1 per tablet — the world's cheapest opioid
- legalStatus: Schedule IV US; Rx-only everywhere; some countries restrict sharply due to abuse epidemics
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: WHO, NIDA, EMCDDA, FDA

## Tapentadol (Nucynta)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/tapentadol/
- aliases: Nucynta, Palexia, Tapal
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule II (US)
- appearance: 50–250 mg tablets; ER versions
- effects: Opioid pain relief plus norepinephrine reuptake inhibition — tramadol's stronger cousin; Faster, more predictable than tramadol (no CYP2D6 lottery)
- risks: Schedule II for a reason: full mu-opioid addiction profile; Seizure risk lower than tramadol but present at high doses; Serotonin syndrome in combination; Withdrawal standard opioid — rough
- overdoseSigns: Pinpoint pupils; Slow breathing; Sedation
- streetPrice: ~$1–$5 per tablet diverted
- legalStatus: Rx-only, Schedule II US; controlled everywhere
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, EMA

## Loperamide (Imodium) Abuse
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/loperamide/
- aliases: Imodium, Lope, Poor man's methadone, The super loperamide
- category: Opioids
- schedule: OTC — unrestricted; bulk purchases monitored in some US states
- appearance: 2 mg anti-diarrhea tablets, blister packs; users take 50–300+ tablets
- effects: At 100+ mg crosses into the brain: weak opioid calm, withdrawal relief for hours; OTC, cheap, no prescription, no questions
- risks: CARDIAC DEATH — the signature: mega-doses block cardiac sodium/potassium channels → arrhythmia, QT prolongation, sudden death. Multiple documented fatalities; Not a safe withdrawal tool — the dose that stops withdrawal approaches the dose that stops the heart; With P-gp inhibitors (quinidine, some antihistamines) brain penetration multiplies; The 'loperamide challenge' online advice has killed people
- overdoseSigns: Racing irregular heartbeat; Fainting; Seizures; Sudden cardiac arrest
- streetPrice: ~$5–$12 per pack of 18–42 tablets — the accessibility is the danger
- legalStatus: OTC everywhere; several US states restrict bulk sales; FDA issued warnings (2016, 2018)
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, NIDA, PubMed

## Brorphine
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/brorphine/
- aliases: Purple heroin component, Brorph
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule I (US, 2021 temporary → permanent)
- appearance: White/off-white powder, often purple-tinted when mixed ('purple heroin')
- effects: Potent fentanyl-adjacent opioid: strong sedation, euphoria, long duration
- risks: Drove the 2020–2021 'purple heroin' wave — linked to overdose clusters across the US Midwest; Potency ~ fentanyl-scale; mixing errors fatal; Reversed by naloxone but may need high/repeat doses; Often present with fentanyl, xylazine, or medetomidine in the same bag
- overdoseSigns: Respiratory depression; Blue lips, unresponsive; Pinpoint pupils
- streetPrice: Sold as heroin/fentanyl — $10–$40 per bag
- legalStatus: Schedule I US; controlled internationally
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: DEA, NIDA, NPS-AD

## AH-7921
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/ah-7921/
- aliases: Legal heroin, Doxylam
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Schedule I (US, 2015); Class A UK
- appearance: White/off-white powder or tablets; sold online as 'research chemical' around 2013–2015
- effects: Morphine-like opioid synthesized in the 1940s; ~80% of morphine's potency; Short history as a 'legal high' before scheduling
- risks: Multiple UK deaths 2014–2015 (detected alongside etizolam and other NPS); Standard opioid overdose profile; The case that ended the UK's 'legal high' tolerance — led directly to the PSA 2016
- overdoseSigns: Respiratory depression; Pinpoint pupils; Unresponsive

## MT-45 (IC-6)

## W-18
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/w-18/
- aliases: W-18, The '10,000× morphine' myth
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Analogue prosecutions (US); Schedule I Canada
- appearance: White powder — 1980s compound sold as 'research chemical' mid-2010s
- effects: Marketed as a 'designer opioid'; early reports claimed 10,000× morphine
- risks: THE MISINFORMATION CASE: later peer-reviewed testing found W-18 has WEAK opioid activity — the '10,000×' claim was a citation error that panicked 2015–2016 media; Still dangerous as unknown-powder contamination; Lesson: potency claims on grey-market drugs are often marketing
- overdoseSigns: Unknown pharmacology — treat any unresponsive opioid-like event with naloxone
- streetPrice: N/A — historic scare compound
- legalStatus: Analogue Act US; Schedule I Canada
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: PubMed, NPS-AD, EMCDDA

## Naloxone (Narcan)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/naloxone/
- aliases: Narcan, Kloxxado, Nyxoid, The opioid antidote
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Not controlled — OTC (US 2023+); Rx/OTC varying elsewhere
- appearance: 4 mg nasal sprays (Narcan), 8 mg (Kloxxado), 0.4–2 mg injectable ampoules, auto-injectors
- effects: STrips opioids from receptors in 2–3 minutes — reverses overdose breathing within minutes; No effect on non-opioid drugs; no high; safe to give even if unsure
- risks: Short half-life (30–90 min) vs fentanyl's hours — the person CAN RE-OVERDOSE as it wears off. Stay and repeat; Precipitates withdrawal in dependent users — expect anger, vomiting, pain (they're alive — that's the point); Higher-potency opioids (nitazenes, carfentanil) may need 4–10+ doses; Does NOT reverse xylazine (but still give it for the fentanyl half)
- overdoseSigns: (Overdose signs it treats): unresponsive, pinpoint pupils, slow/gurgling breathing, blue lips
- streetPrice: US OTC ~$45 (Narcan); FREE via nextdistro.org, syringe services, most harm-reduction programs; pharmacies Canada/UK/AU
- legalStatus: OTC US (2023); UK drug services; most countries allow possession for overdose response; Good Samaritan laws protect callers in most US states
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, NIDA, CDC, EMCDDA

## Naltrexone (Vivitrol / Revia)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/naltrexone/
- aliases: Vivitrol, Revia, Depot naltrexone
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Not controlled — Rx-only
- appearance: 50 mg tablets; 380 mg monthly injection (Vivitrol)
- effects: Full opioid BLOCKER — prevents any opioid high for 24 h (tablet) to a month (injection); Also reduces alcohol reward (Sinclair method)
- risks: PRECIPITATED WITHDRAWAL if taken while opioids are in the system — must be fully detoxed first (7–10+ days); Blocks pain relief from opioids in emergencies — carry the Vivitrol card; Overdose risk paradox: tolerance drops during blocking; using through the block escalates doses dangerously; Hepatotoxicity at high doses (historic concern, rare at therapeutic)
- overdoseSigns: (Rare alone) nausea, headache; the danger is the post-treatment relapse overdose
- streetPrice: ~$1–$3 per tablet; injection $1,000+ (insurance covers in US)
- legalStatus: Rx-only everywhere; standard medication for opioid and alcohol use disorder
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, EMA, SAMHSA

## MDA (Sass / Sally)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/mda/
- aliases: Sass, Sass-a-frass, Sally, The Love Drug
- category: Empathogens
- schedule: Schedule I (US); Class A UK
- appearance: White/off-white powder, crystals ('sass'), or pressed pills (often with logos)
- effects: MDMA's more psychedelic parent: empathy + energy + visuals at higher doses; 6–8 h; More dopamine push than MDMA — more stimulating
- risks: MORE neurotoxic than MDMA — harsher serotonin damage at equivalent use patterns; Overheating in clubs; the same hyponatremia (water) danger as MDMA; Jaw clenching, muscle tension worse than MDMA; Often sold as or mixed into 'MDMA' pills; Sold as 'Sass' on dark markets — variable purity
- overdoseSigns: Overheating >40°C; Racing heart, seizures; Serotonin syndrome signs
- streetPrice: ~$10–$30 per dose/pill; 'sass' $80–$150/g
- legalStatus: Schedule I US; Class A UK; controlled everywhere
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: NIDA, DEA, EMCDDA

- risks: Serotonin release + MAO-B activity — serotonin syndrome risk, especially with antidepressants or MDMA; Cardiovascular strain; overheating; The 'benzofury' brand has covered many compounds — content varies batch to batch; Redose compulsion
- overdoseSigns: Overheating; Racing heart; Agitation, clonus (serotonin syndrome)

## N-Isopropylbenzylamine (N-Iso)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/n-iso/
- aliases: N-ISO, Iso, The meth mimic
- category: Stimulants
- schedule: Not a drug — cutting agent; 'meth-like' appearance
- appearance: Clear/white crystals nearly identical to methamphetamine (that's the point)
- effects: Essentially inactive — the disappointment is the effect; Sold as meth, sometimes with a little real meth on top ('twisted dope')
- risks: THE SCAM: N-iso is the most common meth adulterant — users pay meth prices for inert crystals; Identifying: N-iso is harder, doesn't 'crack back' the same, bitter-numb difference (subtle); Cuts reduce effective dose → users take more → when real meth appears, overdose; Harm reduction: test kits, start small with any new batch
- overdoseSigns: (As adulterant) — none directly; the danger is the unknown real-meth dose in the same bag
- streetPrice: Sold AS meth — $20–$100/g
- legalStatus: Not scheduled as a drug; sale as meth is fraud/prosecuted as such
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, drugchecking services

## Levamisole (Cocaine Cut)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/levamisole/
- aliases: Levamisole, The flesh-rot cut, Cocaine adulterant
- category: Stimulants
- schedule: Not a drug — veterinary wormer; most common cocaine adulterant
- appearance: White crystalline powder — indistinguishable from cocaine in a bag (that's the point)
- effects: No recreational effect — veterinary dewormer added to bulk cocaine
- risks: THE SIGNATURE: levamisole-contaminated cocaine causes agranulocytosis (immune collapse) and skin necrosis — black rotting earlobes, cheeks, limbs documented across the US/EU; Found in up to 70–80% of seized cocaine in peak years (it passes 'taste/numb' tests and adds stimulant heft); Purpura and ear-rot cases cluster — drug-checking services flag it; Treatment: stop exposure; the immune damage usually reverses in weeks
- overdoseSigns: (Not an overdose drug) — warning signs: black/purple skin patches, sores that won't heal, persistent infections, fever
- streetPrice: N/A — it's the bulk in the bag
- legalStatus: Veterinary medicine; its presence in cocaine is what law enforcement measures
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: DEA, EMCDDA, CDC, PubMed

## Coca Leaf (Traditional)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/coca-leaf/
- aliases: Coca, Huamanga?, Erythroxylum coca, Mate de coca
- category: Stimulants
- schedule: Controlled internationally but traditional use legal in Bolivia, Peru, Argentina (UN 2013 amendment)
- appearance: Green dried leaves chewed with lime/ash; coca tea (mate de coca); bags sold in Andean markets
- effects: Mild, sustained stimulation: alertness, altitude-comfort, appetite suppression — 100× milder than cocaine; Cultural and religious core of Andean life for millennia
- risks: LOW acute harm — leaf alkaloid content is ~0.3–1.5% vs refined cocaine; Coca tea triggers POSITIVE drug tests for cocaine metabolites — athletes and workers have failed tests from tea; International law still lists coca leaf (Schedule I Single Convention) outside the Andean exemption — carrying leaf across borders is trafficking; Chewing causes dental wear; lime burn to gums; The UN-vs-Andes dispute is political: the plant itself is not the powder
- overdoseSigns: Practically none at traditional use levels
- streetPrice: ~$1–$5 per bag in Andean markets; coca tea $5–$15 online
- legalStatus: Traditional/legal use Bolivia, Peru, Argentina, Colombia (tolerated); Schedule I internationally — import to US/EU illegal
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: UNODC, WHO, EMCDDA

## LSD (Acid)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/lsd/
- aliases: Acid, LSD-25, Blotter, Tabs, Lucy, Dots, Windowpane
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Schedule I (US); Class A UK; controlled worldwide
- appearance: Blotter paper squares, liquid drops, microdots, gel tabs; often decorated
- effects: 8–12 h visual/mental psychedelic: patterning, synesthesia, ego dissolution at high doses; Energy and mental clarity ('electric'); Microdosing sub-perceptual trend
- risks: Psychological: bad trips, panic, HPPD (persistent visual disturbances) in a minority; Triggering psychosis in predisposed individuals; Not addictive; no known lethal overdose (physically one of the safest); NBOMe sold as acid is the real danger — taste test (bitter/metallic = spit it out); Set and setting drive outcomes
- overdoseSigns: No physical overdose — 'too much' = overwhelming panic/psychosis, duration until it passes; Someone in terror loop: calm space, reassurance, time
- streetPrice: ~$5–$15 per blotter; $80–$200 per sheet of 100
- legalStatus: Schedule I everywhere listed; research expanding (psychedelic therapy trials)
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, MAPS

## 1P-LSD (and analogs: 1cP, 1V, ALD-52)
