## 5-MeO-DMT (Bufo / Toad Venom)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/5-meo-dmt/
- aliases: Bufo, Toad, The God Molecule, 5-MeO
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Schedule I (US); controlled most regions
- appearance: White powder (synthetic or extracted from Sonoran Desert toad glands); smoked/vaporized 5–20 mg
- effects: 5–20 min COMPLETE dissolution: white light, ego death, 'becoming everything' — far stronger per mg than DMT; Bufo retreats popular in Mexico/US
- risks: RETREAT DEATHS: asphyxiation and aspiration — facilitators sometimes restrain or pour water on people mid-experience; several documented fatalities (2018–2025); NOT the same as DMT — bufotenin (5-HO) vs 5-MeO confusion matters; smoking raw toad secretions adds bufotenin load; Deadly combined with MAOIs (harmalas/Syrian rue) — serotonin syndrome; Psychological destabilization: panic, mania in the days after; Toad populations stressed by 'milking'
- overdoseSigns: Loss of consciousness with vomiting (aspiration risk); Panic/struggling during the peak; Serotonin syndrome signs with MAOIs
- streetPrice: Retreat ceremonies $150–$500 per session; powder $50–$150/100 mg
- legalStatus: Schedule I US; Mexico tolerates retreats; toad species protected in some US states
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, MAPS

## Ayahuasca (The Brew)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/ayahuasca/
- aliases: Yagé, Hoasca, Daime, La Purga, Mother Ayahuasca
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Schedule I components (DMT) US; religious exemptions (UDV, Santo Daime); Peru/Brazil traditional-legal
- appearance: Thick brown bitter tea brewed from Banisteriopsis caapi vine + DMT-containing leaves (chacruna/chaliponga)
- effects: 4–6 h visionary ceremony: intense purging (vomit/diarrhea), geometric visions, emotional release; The MAOI in the vine makes the DMT orally active
- risks: THE DEADLY COMBINATION: vine MAOIs + antidepressants (SSRIs/SNRIs/MAOIs) or MDMA = serotonin syndrome — deaths documented at retreats; Hypertensive crisis with tyramine-containing foods (aged cheese, cured meats) around ceremonies; Cardiac events in vulnerable participants; deaths of healthy-seeming users reported 2015–2025; Retreat industry is unregulated — screening and emergency readiness vary wildly; Psychological destabilization after intense sessions ('the vine keeps working for weeks')
- overdoseSigns: Serotonin syndrome: agitation, clonus, fever, confusion; Severe vomiting with dehydration; Chest pain, collapse
- streetPrice: Retreats $500–$3,500 per week; brew itself not retailed legally
- legalStatus: DMT = Schedule I US (religious exemptions exist); traditional use legal Peru/Brazil/Costa Rica retreats; unregulated most of EU
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, MAPS, Poison Control

## San Pedro Cactus (Echinopsis pachanoi)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/san-pedro/
- aliases: San Pedro, Huachuma, Achuma, Giganton, Aguacolla
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Mescaline = Schedule I US; cactus legal to grow (not prepare) in most places; Peru/Ecuador traditional-legal
- appearance: Tall columnar cactus sold at plant markets and botánicas; prepared as a slow-cooked tea/mash
- effects: 6–10 h gentle mescaline journey: warmth, color enhancement, heart-opening — the 'kind grandfather' of psychedelics; Andean ceremonial tradition (huachuma) millennia old
- risks: Nausea/vomiting at onset (the cactus's slime); Same psychological risks as mescaline — panic in unprepared users; Cardiac strain at high doses (mescaline is a phenethylamine stimulant); Drug tourism injuries: hiking on doses at retreat centers; Preparation concentrates the dose unpredictably
- overdoseSigns: No physical lethal dose known; Extreme agitation, vomiting, racing heart at high doses
- streetPrice: Cactus $20–$60 per cutting (legal); retreat ceremonies $100–$400
- legalStatus: Growing the cactus is legal in most of the world; extracting/preparing mescaline is not (US); traditional use protected Peru
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, MAPS

## Ibogaine (Iboga)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/ibogaine/
- aliases: Iboga, Ibo, The Addiction Interruptor, Root bark, TA (total alkaloid)
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Schedule I (US); illegal most EU; unregulated Mexico/New Zealand/Canada-grey clinics
- appearance: Root bark powder (Tabernanthe iboga), HCl extract, or Total Alkaloid; 3–5 g bark or ~15–20 mg/kg
- effects: 12–36 h intense visionary journey + oneiric state (not recreational — most find it grueling); Interrupts opioid withdrawal within hours — the 'addiction reset' claim driving the clinic industry
- risks: CARDIAC DEATHS — the documented killer: QT-prolongation and arrhythmia; multiple clinic deaths, often without proper ECG screening; Deaths have occurred days AFTER treatment (delayed arrhythmia); The 'cure' is a myth: cravings return in weeks-months without integration; post-ibogaine overdose deaths when tolerance resets; Dangerous with methadone (long half-life), cocaine, or cardiac conditions; Unregulated clinics vary from medically serious to dangerous; Noribogaine's long tail: mood effects for weeks
- overdoseSigns: Arrhythmia, fainting (fatal if untreated); Seizures; Ataxia so severe the person cannot walk
- streetPrice: Clinics $3,000–$10,000 per treatment; bark $50–$150/100 g grey-market
- legalStatus: Schedule I US; NZ prescription-only scheme; Mexico/Canada-grey clinics operate; traditional use Gabon
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: NIDA, PubMed, EMCDDA

## Kambo (Frog Secretion)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/kambo/
- aliases: Kambô, Sapo, Vacina do sapo, Phyllomedusa ceremony
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Not a controlled drug — unregulated ceremony product
- appearance: Burned dots on the skin; secretion of the giant leaf frog (Phyllomedusa bicolor) applied to open gates
- effects: NOT psychedelic — an intense purge: 15–40 min of vomiting, sweating, flushing, heart racing, then clarity; Amazonian hunting-ritual origin; biohacker and wellness ceremony trend
- risks: DOCUMENTED DEATHS: cardiac events and severe dehydration at ceremonies (2019–2025 reports); No medical screening at most circles — blood pressure, heart conditions undetected; Unregulated practitioners; 'clean' secretion claims unverifiable; Contradicts medications; dangerous with MAOIs and cardiac drugs; The purge CAN mask real emergencies — collapse is not 'purging'
- overdoseSigns: Collapse, unresponsive; Chest pain, arrhythmia; Dehydration shock
- streetPrice: Ceremonies $50–$300 per session
- legalStatus: Unregulated most places; Brazil permits traditional use; import rules vary
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: PubMed, Poison Control, EMCDDA

## Yopo / Cebil (Anadenanthera Snuffs)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/yopo/
- aliases: Yopo, Cebil, Vilca, Cojoba, Syrian rue partner
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: DMT/bufotenin controlled US; seeds legal to possess most places; Syrian rue (MAOI) restricted some EU
- appearance: Toasted and ground seeds of Anadenanthera peregrina/colubrina, snuffed; combined with Syrian rue (Peganum harmala) in modern use
- effects: Short 30–60 min intense tryptamine snuff experience (bufotenin/5-MeO-DMT/DMT mix); Traditional Caribbean/South American shamanic use
- risks: Syrian rue combination = MAOI — DEADLY with SSRIs and MDMA (serotonin syndrome); Severe nausea/pain at insufflation; mucosal damage from repeated snuffing; Little modern safety data; traditional preparations were purified by skilled practitioners; Bufotenin-loaded snuffs are harsh and unpredictable
- overdoseSigns: Serotonin syndrome signs with MAOIs; Severe vomiting, collapse; Extreme cardiovascular stress
- streetPrice: Seeds $10–$30 per 100 g; rue seeds $5–$15
- legalStatus: Seeds uncontrolled US; active tryptamines Schedule I; harmala alkaloids restricted DE/others
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: NIDA, EMCDDA, Erowid

## Datura (Jimsonweed / Devil's Trumpet)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/datura/
- aliases: Jimsonweed, Devil's trumpet, Angel's trumpet, Thornapple, Locoweed, Malpitte
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Not federally scheduled US (Deliriant); plants controlled some localities
- appearance: Spiky seed pods and trumpet flowers; seeds and teas — every part contains scopolamine/atropine/hyoscyamine
- effects: 12–48+ h TRUE DELIRIUM: conversations with people who aren't there, smoking imaginary cigarettes, complete reality loss; Not a 'trip' — you cannot distinguish the hallucination from reality
- risks: THE TOXIDROME: overheating (can't sweat), racing heart, urinary retention, blindness-level pupil dilation — hospitalizations and ICU stays are COMMON, not rare; Teen dare trend ('Datura challenge' videos) has poisoned thousands; Fatal dose is close to the 'active' dose — deaths from cardiac arrest and hyperthermia; Users routinely hurt themselves or others mid-delirium; police/ambulance encounters; No enjoyable version of this experience exists — veterans call it 'the shadow realm'
- overdoseSigns: Hot dry flushed skin, NO sweating; Racing heart, seizures; Extreme agitation or catatonia; Dilated unresponsive pupils
- streetPrice: Free — grows wild on every continent; seed packs $3–$10
- legalStatus: Unscheduled federally; some US states/plant-sale restrictions; poison-control flagged
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: Poison Control, NIDA, EMCDDA

## Nutmeg (Myristicin)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/nutmeg/
- aliases: Nutmeg high, Myristica, Kitchen spice trip
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Food/legal — unregulated
- appearance: Whole nutmeg seeds or ground spice from the kitchen; 5–20 g consumed
- effects: 5–15 g of myristicin/elemicin metabolized to weak MAO-A-releasing deliriant: 6–24 h of heavy sedation, dreamlike stupor, mild visuals; The original 'kitchen high'
- risks: 24 HOURS of misery is the typical report: racing heart, severe dry mouth, dizziness, anxiety, hangover days long; Overdose: tachycardia, seizures, organ stress — ICU admissions documented; Teen accessibility is the whole story — it's in every pantry; Combining with MAOIs or stimulants dangerous; Not fun, not safe — the data says almost everyone regrets it
- overdoseSigns: Racing heart, chest pain; Severe agitation, hallucinations; Vomiting, dehydration
- streetPrice: $1–$5 per jar — the cheapest 'high' in existence
- legalStatus: Legal food everywhere; poison-control flagged for abuse
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: Poison Control, NIDA

## Morning Glory / Hawaiian Baby Woodrose (LSA)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/morning-glory/
- aliases: LSA, Ergine, Heavenly Blue, Hawaiian baby woodrose, Argyreia nervosa
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Seeds legal to possess most places (not for consumption); LSA itself controlled where DMT-class is
- appearance: Seed packets sold legally as ornamentals; 50–300 morning glory or 3–10 HBWR seeds chewed/extracted
- effects: Ergoline cousin of LSD: 6–10 h sedating, dreamy, nausea-heavy psychedelic; Legal-seed loophole makes it a teen entry point
- risks: SEED COATINGS: commercial seeds are often treated with fungicides/pesticides (mercury-based historically) — wash or source organic; Severe nausea/vasoconstriction (the ergoline body-load); Uterine contraction risk — dangerous in pregnancy; Cyanogenic glycosides in some species; Psychological risks standard for psychedelics
- overdoseSigns: Severe nausea/vomiting; Leg cramps, vascular pain; Agitation at high doses
- streetPrice: Seed packets $2–$6 (legal); HBWR seeds $5–$15 per 10
- legalStatus: Seeds sold as non-consumable; LSA controlled in some countries; extraction = manufacture charges
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: NIDA, Erowid, EMCDDA

## 2C-x Family (2C-E, 2C-I, 2C-C, 2C-D, 2C-P)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/2c-x-family/
- aliases: 2C-E, Aquarust, 2C-I, 2C-C, 2C-D, 2C-P, Europa, Isabel
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Schedule I (US — 2C-B/E/I/P named); Class A UK; controlled EU
- appearance: White powder, pellets, or pressed pills sold as '2C-B' or research chemicals
- effects: Shulgin's phenethylamine family: 2C-E is the 'teacher' (visual, deep, 8-10h); 2C-I more stimulant; 2C-P the long one (10-20 h); Dose-sensitive: 5 mg changes the experience
- risks: 2C-P IS THE KILLER: 10–20 h duration; users redosing thinking it's 'weak' have died ('Beast' deaths in UK 2013); Sold as 2C-B or 'mescaline' — dosing chaos; Vasoconstriction, BP spikes, overheating; Stimulant-load on the heart across the family
- overdoseSigns: Overheating, racing heart; Hallucinations with severe agitation; Seizures
- streetPrice: ~$10–$30 per dose
- legalStatus: Schedule I US (several named); Class A UK; individual bans across EU
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18

## DOx Family (DOB, DOC, DOI)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/dox-family/
- aliases: DOB, DOC, DOI, The 24-hour acid
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Schedule I (US, DOB/DOC/DOI analogs); controlled EU
- appearance: Blotter or powder — the classic 'fake acid' alongside NBOMe
- effects: 24–36 HOUR amphetamine-psychedelic: energy + visuals that just do not stop; DOM (STP) is the family patriarch
- risks: THE TIME TRAP: sold as LSD-sized doses of LSD — a full DOB dose is tiny, and users take 'one more tab' → 36-hour amphetamine psychosis, hospitalizations; Strong vasoconstriction: cold extremities, BP danger; Cardiac strain over the marathon duration; If a blotter takes 3+ hours to work, you may have a DOx — do not redose
- overdoseSigns: Racing irregular heart for hours; Severe agitation, hallucinations; Overheating
- streetPrice: Sold as LSD — $5–$15 per blotter
- legalStatus: Schedule I analog US; controlled EU/UK
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: DEA, EMCDDA, NIDA

## NBOMe (25I, 25C, 25B-NBOMe)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/nbome/
- aliases: 25I-NBOMe, N-Bomb, 25C-NBOMe, Smiles, 25B
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Schedule I (US); Class A UK; controlled EU
- appearance: Blotter with designs mimicking LSD; sometimes powder; bitter metallic taste and tongue-numbing are the tell
- effects: Aggressive phenethylamine psychedelic at MICROGRAM doses — sold as 'strong acid'; 10–20× smaller active dose than LSD
- risks: THE DEATH CLUSTER: 2012–2016 overdose deaths across US/EU/Russia — vasoconstriction so severe it caused strokes, heart attacks, kidney failure; Sold as LSD: users taking '2 tabs' ingest 20+ lethal-equivalent doses; Bitter/metallic taste + mouth numbing = SPIT IT OUT (LSD is tasteless); Seizures, severe aggression, hyperthermia; Survives being swallowed less than LSD — the harm-reduction lore that 'if you swallow it you're safe' is unreliable
- overdoseSigns: Seizures; Racing heart, chest pain, stroke signs; Severe agitation/violence; Hyperthermia, kidney failure
- streetPrice: Sold as acid — $2–$8 per blotter (cheap because it's cheap to make)
- legalStatus: Schedule I US; Class A UK; controlled worldwide
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: DEA, NIDA, EMCDDA

## aMT (alpha-Methyltryptamine)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/amt/
- aliases: AMT, Indopan, IT-290, The tortoise
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Schedule I (US); Class A UK
- appearance: Off-white powder/crystals; historically 5–10 mg antidepressant tablets, now sold as powder
- effects: Long (12–16 h) serotonin-releasing psychedelic-stimulant hybrid: energy + visuals; Sold as 'cheap MDMA' in the 2000s
- risks: SEROTONIN SYNDROME DEATHS — aMT releases serotonin AND blocks its breakdown; combined with SSRIs, MDMA, or DXM it can kill; The 'long tortoise' duration traps anxious users; Sold as MDMA at MDMA doses = overdose; MAOI properties + stimulant load
- overdoseSigns: Agitation, clonus, fever (serotonin syndrome); Racing heart, seizures; Hallucinations 12h+
- streetPrice: ~$15–$35 per dose
- legalStatus: Schedule I US; Class A UK
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: DEA, NIDA, EMCDDA

## Absinthe (Wormwood / Thujone)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/absinthe/
- aliases: Absinthe, The Green Fairy, Wormwood spirit, La Fée Verte
- category: Psychedelics
- schedule: Legal alcohol product (thujone-limited) EU/US; historic bans largely repealed
- appearance: Green anise-flavored spirit at 45–74% ABV; the 'louche' ritual with sugar and water
- effects: Alcohol's effects plus (at historic adulterated doses) thujone's GABA-modulating stimulation — modern legal absinthe is mostly just very strong liquor; The 'green fairy hallucination' legend is mostly myth
- risks: THE MYTH vs THE REALITY: 'absinthism' (hallucinations, madness) was mostly 19th-century adulteration with copper salts/antimony and plain alcoholism — modern thujone limits (35 mg/kg EU) make true thujone poisoning near-impossible from legit bottles; Real risks = 70% ABV alcohol: dependence, poisoning; Grey-market 'thujone-boosted' bottles can exceed limits — seizures reported; Historic bans (Switzerland 1910–2005, US 1912–2007) built the mystique
- overdoseSigns: Alcohol poisoning (the actual risk); Seizures from adulterated/high-thujone products
- streetPrice: $30–$90 per bottle
- legalStatus: Legal with thujone limits (US/EU); historic bans repealed 2000s
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: EMA, FDA, PubMed

## St John's Wort (Hypericum)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/st-johns-wort/
- aliases: SJW, Hypericum perforatum, Amber, Klamath weed
- category: Performance & Grey-Market Pharma
- schedule: OTC supplement — unregulated US; Rx-only Germany for depression
- appearance: Yellow-flowered herb; capsules, teas, tinctures standardized to hypericin/hyperforin
- effects: Mild antidepressant effect for mild-moderate depression (German Rx tradition); The most-studied herbal psychotropic
- risks: THE INTERACTION KING: induces CYP3A4 and P-gp — weakens oral contraceptives (pregnancies documented), HIV antiretrovirals, transplant immunosuppressants, blood thinners, chemotherapy; Serotonin syndrome with SSRIs, MDMA, tramadol; Photosensitivity (livestock poisoning history); The 'natural so safe' assumption is the danger — it is a real psychotropic with real pharmacology
- overdoseSigns: Serotonin syndrome signs with combos; Severe photosensitivity reactions
- streetPrice: $8–$20 per bottle
- legalStatus: Supplement US; Rx Germany; interaction warnings FDA/EMA
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, EMA, PubMed

## Methoxetamine (MXE)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/methoxetamine/
- aliases: MXE, Mexxy, Roffle
- category: Dissociatives
- schedule: Analogue prosecutions (US); Class B UK; controlled EU
- appearance: White/off-white powder; sublingual/intranasal/oral

## SARMs (Ostarine, LGD-4033, RAD-140, S-4)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/sarms/
- aliases: Ostarine, MK-2866, LGD-4033, Ligandrol, RAD-140, Testolone, S4/Andarine, Cardarine, GW-501516, MK-677
- category: Steroids & Anabolics
- schedule: Not approved for human use anywhere; WADA-banned; FDA warnings; 'research chemical' grey market
- appearance: Liquid droppers, capsules, or powders sold as 'research only'; every gym-adjacent website sells them
- effects: Selective androgen receptor modulation: muscle/strength gains weaker than steroids with (claimed) fewer androgenic sides; MK-677 (a ghrelin agonist, not a SARM) boosts appetite/GH
- risks: ZERO human approval — no long-term safety data anywhere; liver enzyme elevations documented; liver injuries reported to FDA; Suppression: they shut down natural testosterone — users need real PCT, which grey-market sellers never mention; Cardarine (GW-501516) caused cancers in rodent studies at human-equivalent doses — the mouse study that killed its development; Sold as 'legal steroids' with fake COAs; most products are underdosed or mislabeled; Vision side effects (yellow tint, night blindness) with S-4; WADA-banned — tested athletes pop hot regularly
- overdoseSigns: Jaundice, dark urine (liver); Severe suppression symptoms: depression, libido collapse; Vision changes (S-4)
- streetPrice: $30–$80 per 30 mL bottle — the gym-shop economy
- legalStatus: Unapproved drug everywhere; WADA-prohibited; FDA warning letters; selling for consumption violates law — 'research' label is the dodge
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, WADA, PubMed

## Prohormones (1-Andro, 4-Andro, Superdrol clones)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/prohormones/
- aliases: 1-Andro, 4-Andro, 1-Testosterone, Androsterone, Epiandrosterone, Helladrol clones
- category: Steroids & Anabolics
- schedule: Many Schedule III (US, Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act 2014); grey 'supplements' persist
- appearance: Capsules and liquids sold in 'muscle builder' packaging at supplement shops
- effects: Weak oral steroids marketed as legal supplements: modest gains, real suppression
- risks: They ARE steroids — liver stress (methylated ones like Superdrol clones cause real hepatotoxicity), shutdown, lipid destruction; The 2014 DASCA banned dozens; post-DASCA 'legal' ones keep getting scheduled one by one; Teens buy them at supplement stores thinking they're safe naturals; No PCT sold alongside = crashed hormones, depression
- overdoseSigns: Jaundice, abdominal pain; Severe BP elevation; Suppression crash
- streetPrice: $30–$70 per bottle
- legalStatus: Schedule III US (named compounds); the 'supplement' category is a moving legal target
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, DEA, PubMed

## Insulin (Bodybuilding Abuse)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/insulin-abuse/
- aliases: R, N, Humalog, Novorapid, Lantus, The most dangerous gym drug
- category: Steroids & Anabolics
- schedule: OTC in some countries (US vials behind pharmacy counter; cheap OTC Canada/Mexico)
- appearance: Vials of rapid (Humalog/Novorapid) or long-acting (Lantus) insulin; U-100 syringes
- effects: Drives glucose into muscle — bodybuilders stack it with HGH/steroids for growth; 'the most anabolic hormone' gym lore
- risks: HYPOGLYCEMIC DEATH is the signature: misdosed or mistimed insulin drops blood sugar — brain damage or death within hours; bodybuilder deaths documented; No margin: a few units' error, missed meal, or unexpected cardio can kill; Often sourced OTC without ANY medical supervision — no glucose meter discipline; The gym-bro 'start at 2 IU' forum dosing has hospitalized thousands; Unlike steroids, insulin is not a 'try it and see' drug — the first mistake can be the last
- overdoseSigns: Shakiness, sweating, confusion (hypoglycemia); Seizures, unconsciousness; Death if untreated — sugar/juice/glucagon immediately if conscious
- streetPrice: $25–$40 per vial OTC where legal
- legalStatus: Rx US; OTC Canada/Mexico/parts of EU; insulin overdose is treated as self-harm/medical emergency
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, EMCDDA, case literature

## Semaglutide (Ozempic / Wegovy / Rybelsus)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/semaglutide/
- aliases: Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus, GLP-1, The skinny jab
- category: Weight Loss & Metabolic Meds
- schedule: Rx-only everywhere
- appearance: Single-dose injection pens (0.25–2.4 mg weekly); oral tablets; a booming counterfeit-pen market
- effects: GLP-1 agonist: appetite collapse, 10–15% body-weight loss — the most effective obesity drug ever made
- risks: COUNTERFEIT PENS EPIDEMIC: 2023–2025 US/UK seizures of fake Ozempic with wrong doses, wrong drugs, and non-sterile needles — buy only from pharmacies; Compounded/gray-market versions: dose variance, contamination; Gastroparesis (stomach paralysis) lawsuits; severe nausea; Muscle loss without protein/resistance training; Boxed warning: thyroid C-cell tumors in rodents; Suicidal-ideation signal under regulator review; Pregnancy contraindicated
- overdoseSigns: Severe vomiting/dehydration; Hypoglycemia (especially with diabetes meds); Pancreatitis pain
- streetPrice: Rx ~$900–$1,300/mo US (covered for obesity); grey 'compound' $150–$400; fakes $50–$200
- legalStatus: Rx-only; counterfeit sale prosecuted; Novo supply shortages drove the fake market
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, EMA, Novo safety communications

## Hashish (Cannabis Resin)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/hashish/
- aliases: Hash, Charas, Charras, Pollen, Kief, Shish
- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Follows cannabis law; illegal most of Africa/Asia/Middle East where it's most consumed
- appearance: Dark brown/black resin blocks (Afghan/Moroccan), soft 'pollen' powder; smoked, eaten, or in tea
- effects: Concentrated cannabis: heavier, more sedating high than flower; the traditional form across Africa, the Middle East, and South Asia
- risks: 2–5× flower potency by weight — easier to overconsume, especially in edibles/tea; Same dependence/psychosis risk profile as high-THC cannabis; Harsh adulterants in street soap-bar hash (historically: henna, boot polish, plastic, benzene residues in smuggled blocks); Severe penalties in the very regions where it's traditional (death in some Gulf/Southeast Asia cases)
- overdoseSigns: Severe anxiety, paranoia; Vomiting (cannabinoid hyperemesis); Fainting
- streetPrice: $5–$15/g traditional markets; $15–$40/g Europe
- legalStatus: Illegal where cannabis is illegal — most of Africa/Asia; tolerated in parts of traditional-use regions
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: UNODC, EMCDDA, NIDA

## THCA Flower (The 'Legal Weed' Loophole)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/thca-flower/
- aliases: THCA hemp flower, Legal bud, Hemp flower high-THCA
- category: Cannabinoids
- schedule: Federally unscheduled (US Farm Bill loophole); state bans spreading; EU novel-food restricted
- appearance: Identical-looking cannabis flower sold in smoke shops and online as 'hemp'; converts to Delta-9 THC when heated
- effects: Smoked/vaped, it IS regular weed — the THCA decarboxylates into Delta-9 THC in the flame; The 2018 Farm Bill's '<0.3% Delta-9' definition created the loophole
- risks: THE LOOPHOLE: shops sell what is functionally marijuana under hemp licenses — police can't distinguish it; enforcement chaos; States are banning it one by one (dozens by 2025); Contaminants in unregulated hemp grows: heavy metals, pesticides, molds; The same impairment, dependence, psychosis risks as cannabis; Drug tests: positive for THC (obviously)
- overdoseSigns: Same as cannabis: anxiety, paranoia, vomiting
- streetPrice: $30–$60 per 3.5 g 'hemp' jar
- legalStatus: Federal loophole US; banned in 20+ states; EU considers THCA-rich flower novel food/controlled gray
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: FDA, state statutes, NIDA

## Nasal Snuff (Dry Tobacco Snuff)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/nasal-snuff/
- aliases: Snuff, Poschl, Toque, Bernard, Schmalzler
- category: Tobacco & Nicotine
- schedule: Legal adult product; EU sale rules; age-restricted
- appearance: Fine dry powdered tobacco in tins; sniffed, not smoked or chewed; centuries-old European tradition
- effects: Fast nicotine hit via nasal mucosa — 5–10 min alertness/calm; no combustion, no spitting
- risks: Still tobacco: nicotine dependence identical to cigarettes; TSNA carcinogens (tobacco-specific nitrosamines) — nasal/snuff cancers documented (classic 'snuff dipper's cancer' of the nose/sinuses); Much lower lung risk than smoking (no combustion) — the honest harm spectrum; Nasal irritation, congestion, sneezing with heavy use; The harm-reduction position: less deadly than cigarettes, not harmless
- overdoseSigns: Nicotine poisoning: nausea, dizziness, vomiting; Racing heart
- streetPrice: $3–$8 per tin (10–25 g)
- legalStatus: Legal adult product in the EU/UK/US; flavored snuff restrictions in some EU states; age-restricted
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: WHO, EMCDDA, NCI

## Poppy Seeds & Poppy Seed Tea
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/poppy-seeds/
- aliases: PST, Poppy tea, Unwashed seeds, The bakery bag high
- category: Opioids
- schedule: Seeds legal (food) US/EU; unwashed-seed tea sits in a legal gray zone; pods controlled
- appearance: Blue-black food-grade poppy seeds; tea brewed from unwashed seeds or dried pods (opium poppy, Papaver somniferum)

- legalStatus: Seeds legal as food; pod possession = opium charges US; unwashed-seed intent is a gray zone actively prosecuted in some cases

## Tusi ('Pink Cocaine')
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/tusi/
- aliases: Tusi, Tucibi, Pink cocaine, Pink powder, 2C-B of the poor (wrongly)
- category: Stimulants
- schedule: Component-dependent (ketamine+MDMA+2C-B analogs); illegal most places
- appearance: Bright pink powder sold in clubs; NOT 2C-B and NOT cocaine — a branded mixture
- effects: The 2023–2025 club scene's branded mystery: typically ketamine + MDMA + caffeine + a 2C-B-family compound + pink dye — a dissociative-empathogen mashup
- risks: THE LIE IS THE BRAND: 'Tusi' implies 2C-B but lab testing shows ever-changing mixtures — users cannot know the stimulant:dissociative ratio; Overdose pattern = stimulant toxidome + ketamine collapse in the same person; Colombia-Miami origin; spread through LatAm, Spain, US festivals; Because it's a 'brand,' users trust batches they shouldn't; Repeat-dose compounding of unknowns
- overdoseSigns: Overheating, racing heart (stimulant side); Catatonic collapse (ketamine side); Confusion between the two slows correct response
- streetPrice: $40–$100 per gram club pricing
- legalStatus: Components illegal; the brand-name gray zone is closing fast
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: EMCDDA, DEA, drug-checking services

- appearance: Orange flower clusters dried and smoked; South African traditional ('wild dagga' = wild cannabis, but no cannabinoids)

- risks: LOW harm itself; The 'cannabis alternative' marketing invites expectation mismatch; Often blended with damiana/kanna — and occasionally sprayed synthetics; Smoked plant matter harms lungs regardless of the herb
- overdoseSigns: None documented
- streetPrice: $5–$15 per ounce
- legalStatus: Legal; sold as incense in many shops
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-18
- sources: Erowid, PubMed

## Mugwort (Artemisia vulgaris)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/mugwort/
- aliases: Mugwort, Dream herb, Artemisia, Sailor's tobacco

## California Poppy (Eschscholzia californica)

- schedule: Legal herb (distinct from OPIUM poppy — different genus entirely)

## Cryolipolysis (CoolSculpting / Fat Freezing)
- url: https://plugreports.com/drugs/cryolipolysis/
- aliases: CoolSculpting, Fat freezing, Cryoslimming, Fat freeze belts
- category: Beauty Industry & Med Spa
- schedule: FDA-cleared device (professional); at-home belts/creams unregulated
- appearance: Clinic paddles that freeze fat pockets (abdomen, chin); also sold as home 'fat freeze belts' and machines on marketplaces
- effects: Freezes ~20–25% of fat cells in a treated pocket over 2–3 months; non-surgical spot reduction
- risks: PARADOXICAL ADIPOSE HYPERPLASIA (PAH): the rare but real 'reverse' — treated fat GROWS back thicker and harder (Linda Evangelista's famous case, filed lawsuit); usually permanent, needs surgery; Home devices: frostbite, permanent tissue damage — no temperature control; Numbness, bruising, pain lasting weeks; Unregulated 'slimming salons' buying machines without training; Weight returns if lifestyle unchanged — the marketing omits this
- overdoseSigns: (Not a drug) — frostbite blisters, paradoxical hardening/enlargement of treated area
- streetPrice: Clinic $600–$4,000 per area; home belts $30–$200
- legalStatus: FDA-cleared for professionals; home devices unregulated; PAH led to litigation
- lastUpdated: 2026-09-20
- sources: FDA, ASPS
